- #802 discusses repeated expensive retries of a failing source.

I did not find an issue or PR tracking this specific terminal-reservation mismatch and persistent no-progress state.

title: One oversized compressed Codex rollout (over the 256 MiB per-leaf limit) blocks the whole Codex route from refreshing
body:
## Summary

A single standard-zstd Codex rollout (`.jsonl.zst`) whose compressed snapshot plus decoded stream exceeds the documented 256 MiB per-leaf limit makes the **whole Codex route** fail as `unreadable` and be carried forward. While that one leaf exists, no new or updated Codex rollouts in the same route are indexed.

## Environment

- ctx 2.2.8 (official managed install), macOS, manual indexing mode
- Codex home with ~5,500 rollouts; 3 of them are compressed leaves above the limit (largest: ~194 MiB compressed / ~351 MiB decoded)

## Reproduction

1. Create an empty data root and a `CODEX_HOME` containing a few normal rollouts plus one oversized `.jsonl.zst` leaf.
2. `ctx import --incremental --provider codex --data-root <root> --format json`
3. Exit code 1. The route outcome is a failure with class `unreadable` / code `malformed_source`, `carried_forward: true`, `retryable: false`. The leaf error is `compressed snapshot and decoded stream exceed the per-leaf temporary-volume limit`.
4. Add a new small rollout to the same `CODEX_HOME` and import again: the route still fails as a whole, and the new rollout is not indexed.

With an existing indexed route, the previous generation's sources are kept (no data loss), but that route never advances.

## Expected

The limit is documented in `limitations`, so rejecting the oversized leaf is fine. The rest of the route should still refresh: report the oversized leaf as a source failure or rejection, and index the other leaves. This would be the same per-leaf isolation as #707 and #1068.

## Also

- For route-level failures, the import receipt reports `source_failures_omitted` and does not include the selector of the failing leaf. We had to bisect the Codex home to find which file caused it. Including the selector, or the decoded and compressed sizes, would make this diagnosable.
- Our current workaround is a separate `CODEX_HOME` mirror in which oversized leaves are replaced by decompressed raw `.jsonl` copies. Raw leaves are not subject to the limit.

title: fix(history): preserve live OMP titles and divergent Cursor views
body:
## Problem

Two live-history cases lose retrieval coverage:

- OMP rewrites its fixed-width leading title record during a conversation. Cursor-independent Pi prefix authentication treats that metadata update as a conversation rewrite and rejects the capture. Reproduced with official 2.2.8; stopping the title writer makes the same 10,000-message input import successfully.
- Cursor can write different ordered histories under the same native session UUID. Selecting only the longest copy discards unique content or an alternative occurrence order. Content-set containment does not establish a shared chronology.

## Changes

- Admit a validated first 256-byte OMP v1 title slot, including LF, as mutable metadata. Normalize only that slot in aggregate authentication; keep the session header and every following byte exact. Bind the hash mode to checkpoint identity and preserve the current complete-record resume frontier.
- Preserve genuine Cursor forks as separately addressable physical views with their own source provenance and event order. Do not merge timelines. Ordinary equivalent/prefix copies retain their existing deduplication behavior until a fork cohort is published.
- Retain an existing canonical view's citations while its backing file remains. Alternatives use native session UUID, root-relative path and configured root identity; an alternative becoming longer does not replace the canonical identity. Named-root relocation preserves the view identities. Removing a canonical backing file retires that view rather than repurposing a surviving alternative's identity.
- Document duplicate common messages, native-UUID lookup ambiguity, and the use of returned ctx session/event IDs to select a view.

## Verification

- Cargo: 330 unit tests across shared JSONL, Cursor/Claude, other JSONL providers and source I/O; 69 JSONL publication tests passed.
- Bazel standard mode: `//crates/ctx-history-read-application:search_show_tests` passed, including the Pi legacy-projection migration. The exact `import_failures::cursor_divergent_transcript_copies_publish_independently_after_convergence` executable contract passed.
- Release CLI smoke: title rewrites during cold/warm OMP import and concurrent 100-message append succeeded; the settled import contained all 10,100 messages.
- Isolated real-Cursor corpus: five preserved views contained all 1,129 projected events. Each complete ordered view exactly matched official 2.2.8 importing that copy alone (including structured tools). Warm migration preserved all 558 previously indexed event IDs; search, exact-view show and a legacy event citation succeeded.
- Independent primary and secondary submission reviews approved the implementation. No functional production changes follow that reviewed candidate; a final contract cleanup removes transient receipt-field assertions rather than changing behavior.

Limits: a broad native-provider contract run timed out at 300 seconds and reported unrelated SQLite/Warp cases in addition to the subsequently fixed receipt-assertion failure. Those unrelated failures have not been baseline-attributed, and this PR does not claim a full-suite pass. The changed Cursor contract was rerun in isolation and passed. Release mode is not used for debug-hook-dependent contracts.

No private transcripts, messages, session IDs, paths or credentials are included in fixtures or this PR. Source histories are read-only; this change does not replace an installed binary.

title: OpenCode selective snapshot materializes oversized cells before the hydration bound
body:
## Summary

In v2.2.8 (`56aaf35233ce7f8aa739c207525a3d67e6ddddbd`), the OpenCode selective SQLite snapshot materializes oversized native `data` cells **before** the adapter's 16 MiB hydration guard. The per-record isolation introduced by #1024 / #1019 works later in the pipeline, but the earlier copy can still require roughly three times the oversized cell's bytes in RSS.

This is per-cell amplification, not database-size-proportional resident memory. No real history is included in this report.

## Synthetic measurement

Linux x86_64, Rust 1.97.1, release build of the unmodified v2.2.8 `ctx-history-source-sqlite` library. A small executable invokes the same `open_selected_tables_snapshot_with_progress` method and six-table allowlist as the OpenCode adapter. Fixture creation runs in a separate process, excluded from the measured child's `wait4().ru_maxrss`.

Each fixture has ordinary OpenCode `session`, `message`, `part` tables/indexes, one valid conversation, and an unrelated `event` table filled with 1 MiB zero blobs. The large-cell variant adds `CAST(zeroblob(370*1024*1024) AS TEXT)` as one legacy `message.data` cell and reduces unrelated padding to keep total DB size comparable.

| DB bytes | oversized data bytes | peak RSS KiB | sampled private snapshot bytes | capture seconds |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 672,010,240 | 0 | 15,784 | < sampling interval | 0.038 |
| 671,879,168 | 387,973,120 | 1,142,484 | 387,940,352 | 1.615 |
| 6,719,696,896 | 0 | 15,784 | < sampling interval | 0.058 |
| 6,719,565,824 | 387,973,120 | 1,141,800 | 387,940,352 | 1.785 |

Scratch is sampled every 5 ms, so these are sampled lower bounds, not exact allocation peaks. All four captures exit successfully. The measurement isolates snapshot acquisition, not complete import/index RSS.

## Code path

- `crates/ctx-history-source-sqlite/src/sqlite_source/snapshot/selective.rs:242-279` selects `rowid, *`, obtains complete native cells, then binds/inserts them. Borrowing avoids a Rust Vec copy but does not avoid SQLite native value/insert record materialization.
- `crates/ctx-history-providers-sqlite-logical/src/providers/opencode/native_path/query/sql.rs:285-305` masks above-bound payloads and records their original length/type only **after** the private copy exists.
- Progress emits only every 4,096 copied rows. A small row-count database with a very large cell can show `source_family_copy` / `snapshot_bytes_completed=0` throughout the expensive copy; that is a separate observability concern.

## Constraints / proposed direction

The generic selected snapshot intentionally promises native value fidelity (`selective.rs:5-8`; `tests/selective.rs:232-260` compares raw bytes and storage classes). Silently nulling/truncating values there would break that contract and can change OpenCode oversized-TEXT versus unsupported-BLOB rejection receipts.

An explicit provider-requested projected-copy policy could mask only OpenCode payload cells at SQL selection time, retain their original byte lengths in typed private metadata, and let existing adapter guards produce the same per-record rejections while retaining valid siblings. The ordinary generic exact-copy API should remain unchanged.

A full-family streaming-copy fallback preserves bytes but restores the repeated whole-DB scratch cost addressed by #1012 / #1088 / #802; incremental blob writes also need care to preserve native TEXT versus BLOB semantics. I am preparing a draft patch with the explicit projected policy and regression coverage so the design can be redirected before merge.

title: fix(opencode): bound payloads before selected snapshot hydration
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1128.

OpenCode's selected SQLite copy hydrates a complete native cell before the existing 16 MiB query guard can isolate an oversized record (#1019 / #1024). This draft applies the bound before copy-time materialization without restoring repeated whole-database copies (#1012 / #1088).

- Add an explicit opt-in projected selected-copy API; generic selected snapshots retain exact native bytes/storage classes.
- Mask only OpenCode payload columns in SQL before hydration. Private metadata preserves original byte lengths and native TEXT/BLOB classes; valid sibling values, rowids and indexes remain intact.
- Projection authority comes from the acquired snapshot, not untrusted native column names. Full-family fallbacks do not claim projected metadata.
- Original lengths drive payload guards, content-byte accounting, role/schema admission, legacy/current overlap proofs and fallback hydration planning. Oversized TEXT and unsupported BLOB rejection receipts remain distinct; masked payloads cannot become searchable content.
- Bump the parser revision and document the Linux acquisition bound. Existing non-Linux/no-write-reader fallback remains unchanged. Provider databases are never modified.

Full-family fallback was considered but would restore whole-DB scratch churn. Silently masking the generic copy would violate its byte/type fidelity contract. This projected policy makes omission explicit and provider-authorized.

## Verified synthetic memory/scratch reduction

Rust 1.97.1, Linux x86_64, release builds of the actual snapshot library, ordinary OpenCode tables/indexes and valid sibling history. Fixture generation runs in a separate process and is excluded from RSS. One 370 MiB native TEXT payload is compared with no oversized payload while unrelated-table padding holds database sizes comparable. No real history is used.

| Fixture | v2.2.8 peak RSS KiB | patched peak RSS KiB | patched private scratch bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ~640 MiB DB, no oversized cell | 15,784 | 15,512 | 40,960 |
| ~640 MiB DB, 370 MiB cell | 1,142,484 | 15,768 | 40,960 |
| ~6.4 GiB DB, no oversized cell | 15,784 | 15,768 | 40,960 |
| ~6.4 GiB DB, 370 MiB cell | 1,141,800 | 15,768 | 40,960 |

The baseline oversized private snapshot sampled ~387,940,352 bytes; patched scratch is read exactly before cleanup. This isolates acquisition RSS, not total import/index resident memory. Source code built from unmodified v2.2.8 also produced a complete release CLI successfully.

## Regression validation

On an isolated Linux worker using `scripts/cargo-diagnostic.sh`:
- Provider library: **114 passed, 0 failed, 3 existing ignored**.
- SQLite-source library: **78 passed, 0 failed**.
- Ordinary/masked scan equivalence across all schema families and indexed/fallback paths proves identical retained records, original byte accounting and rejection classifications. Coverage includes role probes, overlap proofs, native metadata lookalikes, TEXT/BLOB/NULL/numeric/invalid-UTF8 values, sparse rowids, indexes, generic fidelity, source immutability, reserved-name collisions and cancellation cleanup.
- Changed Rust sources formatted with the pinned toolchain.

Owning Bazel checks are not yet green: the first source snapshot had a missing test import (fixed in 5925ca6); docs_check additionally hit the worker's certificate-store configuration while checking an existing external evidence URL. Cargo diagnostics do not substitute for owning Bazel validation. The patched full CLI build and corrected Bazel checks remain pending; this stays draft.

This is intentionally draft so maintainers can redirect the projected-copy metadata design before merge.

title: fix: avoid exhaustive replay after successful member discovery
body:
Fixes #1119.

Creating a session while appending to an existing journal caused a successful member-to-family discovery to be discarded and replayed with exhaustive reconciliation. That replay lost trusted append admission and reread the retained prefix. Accept the already-certified complete inventory instead; keep failure-triggered exhaustive recovery unchanged.

The regression exercises the outer refresh executor with an authored approximately 3.94 MB Codex journal, verifies searchable results, and counts source reads by file identity across reopened handles and workers:

| Change | Existing journal bytes before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Append | 318 | 318 |
| New session | 16,392 | 8,196 |
| Both together | 11,829,095 | 8,514 |
| Both after process restart | 11,829,095 | 8,514 |

New-session reads also fall from 4,556 to 2,278 bytes. These are instrumented logical reads, including buffered read-ahead, not physical storage traffic.

Add separate test-only metadata read operations/bytes for manifests, integrity certifications, active pointers, and Tantivy control files. Warm opens demonstrate nonzero metadata reads even with zero artifact hashing. Document and test that `processed_bytes` measures certified coverage rather than actual I/O.

Validation:

```sh
scripts/bazelw test //crates/ctx-history-refresh-execution:unit_tests //crates/ctx-history-index:unit_tests --config=test --test_arg=--nocapture --test_output=errors
scripts/bazelw test //crates/ctx-history-refresh-execution:unit_tests --config=test --test_arg=maintenance_io --test_arg=--nocapture --test_output=all
scripts/bazelw test //:history_provider_pack_boundary_check //:history_cli_boundary_check --config=test --lockfile_mode=error --test_output=errors
bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci
```

All pass; the full local CI tier passes 268 test targets. The lockfile retains the existing tool dependency pins and updates only the three changed Cargo input fingerprints.

Scope: source-byte coverage targets successful raw Codex JSONL maintenance on Unix and a real process restart. Existing mutation/recovery tests remain; this does not add the full stress/provider matrix or change strict recovery. Metadata accounting is per executing thread and counts successful reads; it excludes failed partial reads and mmap page faults. Provider-specific preflight optimization, metadata caching, and per-leaf failure isolation are separate work.

title: fix: remediate release dependency advisories
body:
The release advisory gate was blocked by expired paste/lru exceptions and 32 additional findings in fresh OSV data. This change remediates lru and all 32 additional findings, retaining only a bounded paste maintenance disposition.

- Upgrade Tantivy 0.26.1 → 0.27.0 and lru 0.16.4 → 0.18.5; remove the lru exception. Preserve index settings and align package audits, SBOM validation, and the candidate manifest contract with the upgraded version.
- Replace both serde_yaml and serde_yaml_ng with `yaml_serde 0.10.7` / `libyaml-rs 0.3.0` across all seven caller crates. Use the canonical dependency name in Cargo, Bazel, and Rust code. Remove the archived `unsafe-libyaml` package and its exception. Add compatibility regressions for MCP edits, APM manifests, saved memory, and existing native/Graphify memory records.
- Upgrade Quinn, rustls, webpki, Tokio, root certificates, ZIP, Sharp, Undici, Vitest/mocker, Vite, and source-map-js to fixed releases. Adapt the ZIP filename API with Office import, format detection, and traversal regressions. Keep Cargo, Bazel, and vendor inventories consistent while preserving diagnostic-tool pins.
- Retain only `paste 1.0.15` / RUSTSEC-2024-0436, owned by `ctx-release-security`, through **2026-10-31 UTC inclusive**. Stable tokenizers and FastEmbed releases retain this compile-time macro dependency; the tokenizer 1.0 prerelease requires an API migration. The exact disposition records callers, residual build-time maintenance risk, and re-review/removal conditions. No scanner ignores or policy exclusions are added.

Validation on merged commit `17dc4f7c6504b81689468f1d7dda02d6e95d6ee3`, including main through `56f33b97e84c79d85249094b7d9769796afc079b`:

- `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci`: passed; 599 build targets and 268/268 test targets.
- Before this main merge, eight owning YAML suites and the manual CLI dependency fixture passed at `c276f07f`: agent integrations, source discovery, graph configuration, graph core, document ingestion, agent application, MCP integration end-to-end, the CLI dependency fixture, and graph CLI memory workflows. These include streaming documents, aliases, merge keys, custom tags, scalar types, malformed input, serialization, and existing memory compatibility.
- Fresh pinned OSV-Scanner 2.4.0 scans passed for all five release target inventories and both in-scope npm locks. Exact clean-head receipts contain one paste disposition and zero expired, unmatched, or unreviewed findings. Every target inventory contains yaml_serde/libyaml-rs and no retired YAML packages.
- Earlier focused advisory-contract, index, ZIP, package-audit, and SBOM suites passed. An isolated compatibility smoke searched an index created by ctx 2.2.8 without rewriting its lexical index files.

These five advisory inventories do not constitute native execution qualification on all five platforms. The installer suite passed 347 tests with 74 platform/tool skips; PowerShell/native Windows installer coverage was unavailable locally.

Advisory references: [lru](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0253.html), [paste](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0436.html), [unsafe-libyaml](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0449.html).

title: fix: idle after refresh admission failures
body:
A refresh failure before exact-route admission could retain a terminal queue reservation. New scheduled work stayed blocked while overdue route deadlines caused repeated no-work timeout wakeups.

Complete the scheduler handoff for every durably failed request, preserving pending terminal writes and failed logical-request status. After a cycle makes no progress, bound otherwise immediate timeout retries to 10 seconds; filesystem/IPC signals can still wake the daemon immediately, and safety reconciliation keeps its deadline.

Regression coverage reaches the actual All-scope admission refusal, verifies later route recovery in both daemon modes, and bounds no-work wakeups while a foreground query prevents admission. The baseline reproduction hit 32 consecutive no-work cycles with 32 zero-duration waits. The bounded-wait test now advances through 30 simulated seconds in three cycles with zero immediate timeout wakeups.

Validation:
- `scripts/bazelw test //crates/ctx-daemon-service:unit_tests //crates/ctx-history-refresh:unit_tests --config=test`
- `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci`

Fixes #1125

title: Recover generation lease errors without losing history search
body:
History search can report a malformed durable retention lease even when the
failure is in the separate process read-lock coordinator. Both 2.2.7 and 2.2.8
use the same lease formats. This change preserves the underlying coordinator
I/O error and fixes signed Darwin device-ID comparison on ordinary reader opens.
Users affected by that macOS bug recover automatically after upgrading, without
`doctor --repair`. Owner-controlled coordinator permissions and initialization
bytes are also repaired in place without replacing the inode or dropping live
reader locks.

Verified active/previous history remains readable when an optional durable hold
is invalid. `ctx doctor --repair` verifies the active generation under the
publication lock and quarantines a proven-invalid current-version hold,
preserving its exact bytes. The 4 KiB read limit remains: oversized records,
unclassifiable versions, and supported-size future versions are preserved and
block publication so their retained generation cannot be reclaimed.
Valid holds also remain. Repair does not import, reclaim history, start a
daemon, or change indexing mode. Diagnostics name the repair command;
the troubleshooting guide distinguishes recovery in a patched release from
conditional metadata repair on 2.2.8.

Regression coverage uses synthetic persisted state with the released v2
coordinator names, live cross-process locks, damaged holds, valid/future holds,
and manual-mode CLI repair. The future-hold regression covers 480-byte and
4,580-byte version-2 records and a subsequent import writer opening, checking
that the hold, its generation, and the active pointer survive. Repair output
belongs to the existing CLI presentation crate; no size limits were raised.
The rejected-root doctor test starts in manual mode so a periodic refresh cannot
race its healthy baseline assertion.
The reporter's exact trigger is not established; a stock 2.2.7-to-2.2.8 upgrade
was not reproduced.

Validation on Linux: `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passes all 268 test
targets, the full strict Clippy/build stage, and the physical crate-size gate.
The owning generation (77), index (244; one existing ignored), presentation
(185), CLI lifecycle (126), and rejected-root (9) suites pass. ctx is at 20,997
production CLOC against the unchanged 21,000 limit. An existing worker-exit
assertion failed in an earlier full run, then passed unchanged in subsequent
runs. Native macOS and Windows execution has not been performed.

Fixes #1121

title: Show creator-supplied archive origin in local history
body:
Restored conversations now expose the archive creator's origin and view in search, conversation/event details, event enumeration, and locate output. Human output identifies these as creator-supplied labels, not verified machine identities; JSON/JSONL and MCP carry the same optional `archive_provenance` object. Distinct origins retain their existing separate identities.

The archive owner retains declarations in generation-owned source metadata, so queries use the pinned generation without opening archive or provider files. Existing IDs and archive member bytes are preserved. Older imports gain labels after one repeat restore; subsequent unchanged restores remain no-ops. Until enrichment, absent labels do not establish local origin.

Validation: `scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passed build/lint and all 268 test targets. Focused archive, read-application, history CLI, presentation, and CLI archive integration suites passed. Coverage includes identical content under distinct origins, querying after retained archive files are removed, legacy enrichment, and narrow terminal rendering. One unchanged daemon transport test initially returned `Broken pipe`; its suite passed on rerun and final CI passed.

Fixes #1123

title: fix: isolate refused Codex rollout leaves during refresh
body:
Fixes #1126

An oversized compressed rollout or a refused symlinked transcript can currently stop the whole Codex route from refreshing. This change fixes both cases by reporting the offending leaf as a source failure and letting healthy siblings publish, preserving prior indexed content under the existing partial-inventory retention rules.

Codex discovery uses the shared unobserved-quarantine path for symlinks, nonregular selected files, and permission denial. Compressed framing and catalog-probe failures retain their typed diagnostics. Receipts include the leaf selector, and size-limit failures include compressed bytes, the applicable bound, and a lower bound on decoded bytes when decoding began. Directory/root authority, source-change, and systemic failures retain their existing scope.

Successful route publications now clear internal-failure retry checkpoints even when some leaves fail. Retry checkpoints use the application version owned by the workspace manifest in both Cargo and Bazel builds, including Bazel's release configuration, so upgrades rearm previously paused routes. Per-source retry policy and source-change/manual-import rearming remain unchanged.

Symlinks remain refused. A trusted-target-folder setting is intentionally omitted: peer progress does not require following links, and safely admitting targets would require a cross-root authority and race-validation policy beyond a small configuration list.

Quarantine applies only to selected rollout leaves. A refused directory or ambiguous non-leaf entry fails the route instead of silently omitting a subtree. The exhaustive fallback for exact-member source failures remains intact after #1130.

Regression coverage includes cold/warm leaf failures, size diagnostics, repeated sibling progress, retained content, repair, cold directory refusal, and exact-member failure reconciliation. A two-build test passes an untouched paused journal from a compiled `2.2.8` engine through a same-version restart to a compiled `2.3.0` engine and verifies automatic rearming. Fixtures are authored synthetic cases.

Validation on the branch merged with current main: `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passed its build/Clippy stage and all 269 test targets. Eight owning targets also passed, including 1,051 Rust tests and the two-build upgrade scenario. Repository policy and whitespace checks passed.

title: fix(release): repin reproducible macOS 26.2 SDK transport
body:
The Linux release factory pins a licensed SDK transport whose packaging recipe was undocumented. Re-pin macOS SDK 26.2 (build 25C57, Xcode 26.2 build 17C52) to a reproducible archive and document the GNU tar/gzip recipe in the existing factory guide.

The new transport is 101,960,030 bytes with SHA-256 `633818058e889a08e0be4ca985741e8678578af8da9ce1f8a85a6218b452c0fb`. Two independent packs are byte-identical. Full comparison against the installed SDK verified 32,593 regular files, 9,639 directories and 7,249 symlink targets; only nonportable symlink permission bits are excluded. Licensed archive bytes and acquisition records remain in private storage.

Validation: six local Bazel targets passed: `linux_release_factory_tests`, `validate_public_cli_factory_artifact_tests`, `semantic_release_smoke_tests`, `docs_check`, `buildkite_pipeline_check` and `repository_policy_check`. The complete two-file diff was reviewed and passed the managed public-disclosure push guard. No CLI release was built or signed.

title: fix: report scratch-root daemons and expose read-only inventory
body:
A one-off human `search` against a non-managed data root reports on stderr when it launches a persistent background indexer, including when search fails. The notice identifies the root and gives an executable command to select manual mode. The getting-started testing example selects manual mode before setup and explains that a separate index still discovers history from the same home and environment. Automatic indexing and persistent daemon lifetime remain unchanged.

`ctx daemon status --all` lists registered roots and their daemon state in text or JSON, using existing installation discovery and status observation. It performs no configuration migration, permission repair, startup reconciliation, or record cleanup. It takes no exclusive lifecycle or installation locks. Liveness inspection briefly attempts the existing nonblocking shared `daemon.guard` probe and releases any acquired probe lock before returning. The inventory is scoped to the current executable and managed root; graceful shutdown normally removes registrations.

Registrations persist absolute roots at lease acquisition, including foreground daemons started with relative roots. Child launches also pass absolute roots so a leading dash cannot become an option. Inventory remains usable from a different working directory. Invalid or unreadable records produce individual rows containing `error`, `registration_path`, and a null `daemon`; `data_root` is null when unavailable. Legacy relative roots are displayed as unverified without guessing their original directory. Upgrade and uninstall readers retain strict validation.

Notice and inventory rendering live in `ctx-cli-presentation`; discovery and observation stay in daemon crates. Managed roots are compared by resolved identity. Stop commands use `--data-root=VALUE` with shell quoting that preserves spaces, quotes, newline/ESC, and trailing newlines. Regression tests execute the displayed commands and verify that the intended daemon stops.

Validation:

- `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passed on head `5c12a692` merged with main `8d042c754`: **269/269 targets**, including the size gate, strict build/Clippy, and dependency boundaries.
- `ctx` production CLOC is **20,968**, **29 fewer** than merged main `8d042c754` (20,997), and 16 fewer than the original base (20,984). The 21,000 limit is unchanged.
- Seven owning targets passed, including runtime/application/daemon/presentation unit tests, daemon rendering and public help/docs contracts, and formatting.
- All six scratch lifecycle tests passed. The relative-root inventory case covers both search autostart and foreground startup, from another working directory, with malformed and legacy relative records alongside a live daemon. The leading-dash case executes the rendered stop command against a live daemon.
- Read-only regressions preserve config and registration bytes, leave absent roots absent, and observe supervision while its installation lock is held.

Known pre-existing limitations: independent review reproduced `cooperative_daemon_shutdown_does_not_need_its_deleted_socket_path` and `persistent_daemon_release_lifecycle_is_event_driven_and_self_healing` failing 3/3 on clean base `56aaf352` and original PR head `d4201c37`, with matching signatures. Independent review also reproduced a non-UTF-8 data-root serialization panic on the merged base. These remain outside this change; scheduler internals are untouched.

Commands:

```sh
scripts/bazelw test \
  //crates/ctx-daemon-runtime:unit_tests \
  //crates/ctx-daemon-application:unit_tests \
  //crates/ctx-daemon-cli:unit_tests \
  //crates/ctx-cli-presentation:unit_tests \
  //crates/ctx-daemon-cli:daemon_rendering_tests \
  //crates/ctx-cli-contract-tests:cli_public_help_docs_tests \
  //:rustfmt_check --config=test
scripts/bazelw test //crates/ctx-daemon-cli:persistent_daemon_lifecycle_tests \
  --config=test --test_arg=scratch_
bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci
```

Fixes #1124

title: Select portable archive exports by workspace and time
body:
Archive export can now select recent conversations with `--workspace` and paired `--since`/`--until` bounds, without source/session digest conversion. `--preview` shows the selected whole conversations and activity outside the requested scope; an empty selection explicitly reports zero matches and creates no archive.

Selection reuses event-query workspace metadata and half-open timestamp semantics. Workspace matching uses the same ASCII-only folding as search, and workspace and time must match the same event. One pinned generation backs selection, summaries, and writing. Display limits do not limit export membership. Restored roots keep their original creator-supplied origin/view and original member bytes.

Human preview and export receipts escape untrusted origin, workspace, and provider-session metadata before layout, while JSON retains exact values. Human timestamps use the terminal time zone, typed selection failures retain their error codes, and SQLite owns temporary selection-file cleanup on interruption.

The archive format is unchanged. Separate preview and export invocations recompute their selections. Workspace metadata is evidence of scope, not semantic topic detection, and untimed events cannot match a time range.

Validation: six owning archive/query/history CLI/presentation and CLI archive suites passed. `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passed build/lint, the size gate, and all 269 test targets. Coverage includes same-event conjunction, whole-session expansion, empty and interrupted selections, generation pinning, more than 10,000 matching events, preview truncation, mixed origins, Unicode workspace separation, real SIGINT cleanup, and safe preview/export text with exact JSON after archive restore.

Fixes #1122

title: test: acknowledge legacy refresh before running work
body:
The legacy-owner compatibility test intermittently failed with `Broken pipe (os error 32)` because it performed the entire refresh synchronously before acknowledging admission. When that work exceeded the client’s two-second IPC deadline, the fixture wrote its response to a closed socket.

Acknowledge admission immediately and run the real refresh on a worker after the first status poll confirms receipt of the acknowledgment. Preserve exactly one admission, same-request status observations and terminal receipt checks for exhaustive refresh. Incremental requests still receive one strict rejection without retries, status queries or exhaustive fallback. Production behavior and timeouts are unchanged.

Validation after merging current main (`6d767e0d26a76af49acc74a9a709758ec44160dc`):

- Five uncached runs of `//crates/ctx-daemon-service:unit_tests`: all 296 cases passed in every run.
- All 34 affected targets passed (31 executed, three cached), including formatting and dependency-boundary checks.
- The aggregate `//:repository_policy_check` target passed separately.
- A controlled three-second refresh delay reproduced the original broken pipe and passed with the corrected fixture during the initial diagnosis. The diagnostic delay is absent from this patch.

title: release: prepare ctx 2.3.0
body:
Prepare ctx 2.3.0 by aligning the workspace version, its 64 inherited Cargo lock entries, and all versioned plugin/catalog manifests. Refresh generated Bazel Cargo metadata while preserving existing third-party and diagnostic-tool versions. No runtime behavior changes.

The security remediation from #1131 is already on main. Its bounded `paste 1.0.15` disposition through October 31, 2026 UTC remains unchanged.

Validation: local `bash scripts/check.sh --mode=ci` passed all 269 test targets; all six required Linux SDK groups passed with zero group skips. Focused docs/plugin metadata, repository policy, release target, advisory-input and SBOM checks also passed. The required Swift SDK group passed on macOS (30 tests, one expected platform skip).

title: release: account for reformatted lifecycle regression in source continuity
body:
Release source continuity rejects the historical lifecycle capture fix `baa4d1caaaa29a6c47663a2022fbce58b1b3a55e` because #1137 reformatted one statement. Add its reviewed disposition: the only non-reversing hunk is a token-identical rustfmt line split; the pipe-backpressure capture helper, its tests and the rest of the released patch remain present.

Only one policy entry changes. The checker and all other policy entries remain unchanged. Restoring the historical one-line statement fails the pinned Rust 1.97.1 formatter, which requires the current split.

Validation on `9c0e7bfe153bedb50f42144b7ca33916ba008bac`:

- The unchanged continuity checker passes against all 39 published stable release tags, accounting for 23 nonancestor or required commits; all 22 other entries remain accepted.
- The actual managed-envelope preflight's continuity subprocess exits 0. Its subsequent factory check correctly rejects artifacts bound to the previous source; this is not a full release-preflight pass.
- Four owning release/policy targets pass. All 26 graph-selected affected CI targets pass again on the clean committed tree with `--lockfile_mode=error`.
- The current lifecycle file passes pinned rustfmt. Repository policy and the managed public-disclosure push guard pass.

title: Commit attribution is dropped for primary Claude Code and Pi sessions by `producer_authority_disposition`
body:
Context: ctx 2.3.0 (v2.3.0 permanent links). The reproduction below was run in isolated
data roots (`CTX_DATA_ROOT` + `--data-root`), with synthetic provider transcripts and a real
local git repository at `/tmp/repo` (remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`). Each
scenario executes a real `git commit -m "..." && git rev-parse HEAD` and its real stdout is
placed into the transcript's tool output, so the commit OID is locally resolvable and the
output satisfies the documented exact-result shapes (a single `[branch short-oid] subject`
receipt line and a single full-OID line at end of output).

### Problem

`producer_authority_disposition` gates which provider records may carry positive producer
authority ([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/producer_authority.rs#L56-L230`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/producer_authority.rs#L56-L230)).
The only providers with an exact contract are codex (primary + root, #1102) and, for
current contracts or released child contracts, mux / openclaw / crush / opencode / zed /
gemini ([`#L104-L173`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/producer_authority.rs#L104-L173)).
Claude and Pi have no branch at all, so their records always return
`AbstainUnknown` ([`#L175-L230`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/producer_authority.rs#L175-L230)).
`apply_authority_disposition` then removes every fact type that may confer producer
authority ([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/repositories.rs#L33-L38`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-attribution-derivation/src/core_materialization/repositories.rs#L33-L38)),
including `git.commit.produced`, so `exact_commit_evidence_events` stays 0 and all three
blame availability flags stay false.

This is the same filter #1102 fixed for codex primary sessions; Claude Code and Pi were
left excluded.

The Claude parser itself captures the full evidence chain: `tool_use` rows become an
activity with a `provider_call_id` and an invocation, and the matching `tool_result` row
becomes a linked result
([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-history-provider-claude-cursor/src/claude/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L399-L474`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-claude-cursor/src/claude/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L399-L474)).
The loss happens strictly at the authority gate, after parsing.

### Reproduction

1. `git init /tmp/repo`, add remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`, stage a file.
2. Run the real command `git commit -m "s1: diagnostic commit" && git rev-parse HEAD`;
   capture its combined stdout (a `[main <short>] s1: diagnostic commit` receipt line,
   diffstat lines, and a final full 40-hex OID line).
3. Write a synthetic Claude Code transcript `~/.claude/projects/-tmp-repro/<uuid>.jsonl`
   with one assistant row containing
   `{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_1","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"git commit -m \"s1: diagnostic commit\" && git rev-parse HEAD"}}`
   and one user row containing
   `{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_1","is_error":false,"content":"<captured stdout>"}`.
   Rows carry `sessionId`, `cwd: "/tmp/repo"`, `gitBranch`, `version`, RFC3339 `timestamp`.
4. `ctx import --provider claude --path ~/.claude/projects/-tmp-repro --data-root <fresh root>`
   (the provider authority root is the directory).
5. `ctx status` reports `attribution.currentness = "current"`,
   `materialized_coverage = "complete"`, but
   `coverage.exact_commit_evidence_events = 0` and `availability.commit_blame = false`.
6. `ctx show event` on the two tool rows shows both events with the same
   `provider_call_id` (`toolu_1`), the invocation (tool `Bash`, arguments present), and the
   result (text present) — the parsed chain is complete.
7. `ctx blame commit <oid> --format json` returns
   `{"error":"resource_not_found","reason":"target_not_indexed"}`.

Control: the same repository, command, and output placed in a minimal codex rollout
(`session_meta` without `forked_from_id`, plus `function_call`/`function_call_output` with
a JSON-string `arguments` for `exec_command`) imported into its own fresh data root yields
`availability.commit_blame = true`, `coverage.exact_commit_evidence_events = 1`, and
`ctx blame commit <oid>` returns an attribution of `possible` with a
`possibly_produced_by` match. The only difference between the two runs is the provider.

### Expected behavior

Primary-session records from Claude Code (and Pi) should retain production evidence when
the native command and its successful linked result establish the commit operation, the
same way codex primary records are retained since #1102. Keeping the copied-history and
ambiguous-origin checks is fine; requiring membership in a fixed provider/revision
allowlist that simply has no Claude or Pi entries is what makes commit blame permanently
unavailable for these providers.

title: Pi parser misses tool calls nested in `message.content[]`, so Pi sessions never produce invocation activity
body:
Context: ctx 2.3.0 (v2.3.0 permanent links). The reproduction below was run in isolated
data roots (`CTX_DATA_ROOT` + `--data-root`), with synthetic provider transcripts and a real
local git repository at `/tmp/repo` (remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`). Each
scenario executes a real `git commit -m "..." && git rev-parse HEAD` and its real stdout is
placed into the transcript's tool output, so the commit OID is locally resolvable and the
output satisfies the documented exact-result shapes (a single `[branch short-oid] subject`
receipt line and a single full-OID line at end of output).

### Problem

`pi_activity` looks for the call id only at the top level of the message object
(`toolCallId` / `tool_call_id` / `callId`)
([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L749-L811`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L749-L811),
call-id lookup at [`#L755-L761`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L755-L761),
invocation gate at [`#L767`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs#L767)).
Current Pi session files (session header `"version": 3`) store assistant tool calls nested
inside `message.content[]` as elements of `{"type":"toolCall","id":...,"name":...,"arguments":{...}}`;
the message object itself has no top-level call-id field. Tool results *do* keep
`toolCallId` at the top level of their message object.

As a result the parsed tool-call event has no `provider_call_id` and no invocation, while
the tool-result event has a `provider_call_id` and a result that can never be joined
(the repository-evidence join only links a result when its invocation arrives, see
[v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-repository-evidence/src/core_adapter.rs#L84-L222`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-repository-evidence/src/core_adapter.rs#L84-L222)).
Every Pi commit therefore stays invisible to blame even before the producer-authority
gate (see #1142) is considered.

### Reproduction

1. Repository setup as in #1142 (`git init /tmp/repo`, remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`); run
   `git commit -m "s2: diagnostic commit" && git rev-parse HEAD` for real and capture stdout.
2. Write a synthetic Pi session file
   `2026-10-26T00-00-00-000Z_<uuid>.jsonl` (session header `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"<uuid>","cwd":"/tmp/repo"}`)
   with:
   - a user message row;
   - an assistant message row whose `message.content` contains
     `{"type":"toolCall","id":"call-pi-1","name":"bash","arguments":{"command":"git commit -m \"s2: diagnostic commit\" && git rev-parse HEAD"}}`
     (no top-level `toolCallId` on the message);
   - a result row with `message.role == "toolResult"`, top-level
     `"toolCallId":"call-pi-1"`, `content:[{"type":"text","text":"<captured stdout>"}]`.
3. `ctx import --provider pi --path <file> --data-root <fresh root>`.
4. `ctx show event` for the tool-call event shows `activity` with only literal facts —
   no `provider_call_id`, no invocation. The tool-output event shows
   `provider_call_id = "call-pi-1"` and a result whose text contains the receipt line and
   the final full OID, but it is never joined.
5. `ctx status`: `exact_commit_evidence_events = 0`, all availability flags false.
6. `ctx blame commit <oid>` returns `target_not_indexed`.

For comparison, the parser's own unit fixtures use the older flat shape with a top-level
`toolCallId` on `toolResult` messages, which is why result capture works while invocation
capture does not.

### Expected behavior

The Pi parser should read the tool call identity from `message.content[]` elements with
`type == "toolCall"` (`id` / `name` / `arguments`) and emit an invocation activity joined
to the matching top-level `toolCallId` result, so Pi sessions produce joinable
invocation/result pairs like the other JSONL providers.

title: Codex code-mode `exec` calls (`custom_tool_call`) bypass exec-command extraction and lose their result text, so code-mode commits are unreachable from blame
body:
Context: ctx 2.3.0 (v2.3.0 permanent links). The reproduction below was run in isolated
data roots (`CTX_DATA_ROOT` + `--data-root`), with synthetic provider transcripts and a real
local git repository at `/tmp/repo` (remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`). Each
scenario executes a real `git commit -m "..." && git rev-parse HEAD` and its real stdout is
placed into the transcript's tool output, so the commit OID is locally resolvable and the
output satisfies the documented exact-result shapes (a single `[branch short-oid] subject`
receipt line and a single full-OID line at end of output).

### Problem

Codex's code-mode (collaboration) mode records command executions differently from the
standard `function_call` shape: the invocation is a `custom_tool_call` with the native
tool name `exec` and a JavaScript wrapper in `input`, e.g.

```js
const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd: "git commit -m \"...\" && git rev-parse HEAD",
  workdir: "/tmp/repo",
  yield_time_ms: 1000,
  max_output_tokens: 3000
});
text(r.output);
```

and the paired result is a `custom_tool_call_output` whose `output` is an *array* of
`{"type":"input_text","text":...}` items (a `Script completed\nWall time ...\nOutput:\n`
preamble followed by the command output). Both shapes are taken from real producer
rollouts (originator `codex_exec`, CLI 0.164.0) and are the dominant shapes there.

The nativepath reader does admit these rows — `custom_tool_call` is retained as a tool
call and `custom_tool_call_output` as an excluded result
([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/record.rs#L599-L607`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/record.rs#L599-L607)),
and the projected invocation keeps the call id and captures `input` as the arguments
([`rows.rs#L389-L400`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/rows.rs#L389-L400)).
But the record then breaks in two independent places:

1. **Command extraction never runs.** With no protocol/server, the projected tool is the
   advertised name verbatim ([`rows.rs#L401`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/rows.rs#L401),
   identity passthrough at [`#L480-L501`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/rows.rs#L480-L501)),
   i.e. `exec`. `exact_codex_exec_command` only extracts `cmd`/`workdir` when
   `invocation.tool == "exec_command"`
   ([v2.3.0, `crates/ctx-repository-evidence/src/core_adapter.rs#L291-L293`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-repository-evidence/src/core_adapter.rs#L291-L293)),
   so for `exec` it returns `NotApplicable`: the JS wrapper is never unwrapped, and the
   tool-call event carries only a `session_cwd` fact — no `command`, no `tool_workdir`.
   (Even if the tool name matched, the wrapper is JavaScript, not the JSON object that
   [`#L297-L308`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-repository-evidence/src/core_adapter.rs#L297-L308)
   requires.)
2. **Result text is not captured.** The result text capture accepts only a bare JSON
   string ([`rows.rs#L448-L453`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.3.0/crates/ctx-history-provider-codex/src/codex/nativepath/rows.rs#L448-L453));
   the code-mode `output` array yields `text: {"capture_status":"absent"}` (the raw array
   survives only in `structured_content`), so the linked-outcome evidence paths that read
   the result text (receipt line / final full-OID line) cannot fire either.

The invocation and result do join on the shared call id, but with no command facts and no
result text, `exact_commit_evidence_events` stays 0 and every code-mode commit is
unreachable from `ctx blame commit`.

### Reproduction

1. Repository setup as in #1142 (`git init /tmp/repo`, remote `https://github.com/example/repo.git`); run
   `git commit -m "s3b: diagnostic commit" && git rev-parse HEAD` for real and capture stdout.
2. Write a minimal codex rollout with the real code-mode shapes: a `session_meta`
   (`originator: "codex_exec"`, `cli_version`, `cwd`), a user message, a
   `response_item` with `payload.type == "custom_tool_call"`
   (`status:"completed"`, `call_id:"call_<hex>"`, `name:"exec"`, `input` set to the JS
   wrapper text above), and a `response_item` with
   `payload.type == "custom_tool_call_output"` (same `call_id`, `output` set to the
   two-item `input_text` array described above, second item = the captured stdout).
3. `ctx import --provider codex --path <rollout> --data-root <fresh root>` — import
   succeeds with no rejections.
4. `ctx show event` on the two imported tool events: the tool-call event has a
   `provider_call_id` and an invocation (`tool: "exec"`, arguments present as the JS
   text) but its activity facts contain only `session_cwd`; the tool-output event has
   the same `provider_call_id` and a joined result whose
   `text` is `{"capture_status":"absent"}` (the output array is in
   `structured_content`).
5. `ctx status`: `exact_commit_evidence_events = 0`, `availability.commit_blame = false`;
   `ctx blame commit <oid>` returns `target_not_indexed`.

Control: an identical rollout skeleton (same `session_meta`, same user message, same
timestamps) that differs only in the call shape — `function_call` with
`name: "exec_command"`, a JSON-string `arguments`
(`{"cmd":"git commit -m \"...\" && git rev-parse HEAD","workdir":"/tmp/repo"}`) and a
`function_call_output` whose `output` is the bare stdout string — yields
`exact_commit_evidence_events = 1` and `ctx blame commit <oid>` attribution `possible`
(`possibly_produced_by`). The only difference is the code-mode vs standard call shape.

### Expected behavior

Code-mode tool calls should feed the same bounded, exact exec-command extraction:
`custom_tool_call` invocations with name `exec` should have the first
`tools.exec_command({cmd, workdir, ...})` object literal in the JS `input` unwrapped
(with the same byte/emptiness bounds applied to the extracted values), and the paired
`custom_tool_call_output` should derive result text from its `input_text` items (or
otherwise expose them to the receipt / full-OID result checks), so that commits made
through code-mode carry the same command/workdir/result evidence — and are attributable
from `ctx blame commit` — as standard `exec_command` calls.

title: Pi importer: one non-session JSONL under the sessions root fails the whole Pi route
body:
## Summary

`ctx 2.3.0` refuses to index **any** Pi session when `~/.pi/agent/sessions` contains a `*.jsonl` that is not a Pi session. In my case that is the subagent transcript that the `pi-subagents` extension writes to `<session-dir>/subagent-artifacts/<run>_delegate_<n>_transcript.jsonl`. The whole Pi route fails as `unreadable`:

```
pi: invalid capture payload: Pi source has no valid session header within the bounded identity probe
```

Previously indexed Pi history stays searchable, but no new Pi session is indexed until that unrelated file is moved out of the tree.

## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- ctx 2.3.0, source commit `0e1b92ab6e835866eb7e5e5bd79c76d329cc1a3f`, hosted installer, `stable` channel
- indexing mode irrelevant (reproduced with `ctx import --provider pi` in the foreground, manual mode)
- Pi root holds 93 `*.jsonl` files, of which exactly one is a subagent transcript
- `ctx doctor` reports `History refresh is partial` with detail `pi: invalid capture payload: Pi source has no valid session header within the bounded identity probe`

## Reproduction

1. `mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/sessions/proj/subagent-artifacts`
2. Put a valid Pi session file below `~/.pi/agent/sessions/proj/`.
3. Write `~/.pi/agent/sessions/proj/subagent-artifacts/x_delegate_0_transcript.jsonl` whose first record is a subagent transcript record and not a session header, e.g.:

   ```json
   {"version":1,"recordType":"message","source":"foreground","runId":"2e9e2c88-…","…":"…"}
   ```

4. `ctx import --provider pi`:

   ```text
   Source 1  /Users/<me>/.pi/agent/sessions (pi, unreadable, retained prior data):
   invalid capture payload: Pi source has no valid session header within the bounded identity probe
   ✗ 1 import source failed
   ```

Moving that one file out of the tree makes the same command succeed; in my run it then imported 6 additional sources and 354 searchable events, and the route stayed healthy.

## Cause

`crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs` (`PiJsonlAdapter::discover`) walks **every** `*.jsonl` below the Pi root through `visit_native_jsonl_files`. For each file `probe_records_until(..., MAX_HEADER_PROBE_RECORDS, …)` returns `None` when no session header is found, and that is mapped to

```rust
CaptureError::InvalidPayload(
    "Pi source has no valid session header within the bounded identity probe"
)
```

which fails the route instead of rejecting that leaf.

## Expected

A file that is not a Pi session should be a record- or leaf-local rejection, not a route failure. Any of these would fix it:

- skip `subagent-artifacts/` (or any directory named `subagent-artifacts`) during Pi discovery;
- treat an unrecognized first record as a per-leaf rejection, the way oversized Codex leaves are isolated by #1135 instead of failing the whole route;
- gate the identity probe on Pi's own session file-name shape (`<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl`) rather than on every `*.jsonl`.

This is a recurring breakage rather than a one-off: `pi-subagents` recreates such a transcript whenever a delegated child agent runs in a project directory, so a Pi route that works today breaks again after the next subagent run.

Local workaround I am running: a wrapper that moves `*/subagent-artifacts/*.jsonl` (when the first line is not a session header) out of the Pi root before `ctx import`.

## Related

- #621 / #622 — earlier Pi header-probe problems (title metadata before the session header)
- #1135 — the analogous per-leaf isolation fix for Codex

title: Automatic maintenance sustains 1–2 cores while two harnesses append: live journals re-read (210–312 MB per cycle) and every delta republishes the generation
body:
## Summary

With automatic indexing on 2.3.0 and two agent harnesses appending concurrently, background maintenance never becomes idle: the daemon sustains about one core, with bursts to 2.3 cores, for as long as the appends continue. Each cycle re-reads the journals that are live (measured 210–312 MB of `processed_bytes` per cycle against ~4 KB/s of real appends) and publishes a new full generation, then immediately starts the next cycle.

2.2.8 behaved the same way (88–127 % CPU for 23 hours). The 2.3.0 fixes for the idle loop (#1132 / #1125), Codex prefix re-reads (#1130 / #1119) and oversized Codex leaves (#1135) do not cover this path.

The same corpus with **no live appends** costs almost nothing: a foreground `ctx import --incremental` takes 16–21 s wall and **1.4 s user CPU**, and an immediate repeat run is a no-op. So the steady-state cost is in the live-append path, not in publication alone.

## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon, APFS; ctx 2.3.0 source commit `0e1b92ab…`, hosted installer, `stable` channel
- `[indexing] mode = "auto"`, persistent daemon in full mode, semantic disabled, blame ready
- 2,100 sources / 1,692 sessions / ~275 k searchable events / 3.4 GiB certified source bytes
- lexical generation: **9.5 GiB, 75 segments, 285,156 documents**
- live inputs during the measurement:
  - four Codex Desktop journals, 55.1 MB, 26.9 MB, 25.0 MB, 22.3 MB, each appending about 1 KB/s;
  - one Pi session appending a few KB per tool call.

## Observed

**CPU.** Sampled from `ps -o time=` deltas every 5 s for 150 s: about 154 CPU-seconds (≈1.0 core sustained), samples between 88 % and 108 %, bursts to 231 % / 236 % around commit and pointer publication. A second run over 5 minutes showed the same shape (80–285 %).

**Cycles never stop.** `~/.ctx/daemon/jobs/core-refresh.json`:

| time | phase | processed_bytes | elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19:24:02 | refreshing | 950,967 | 1.2 s |
| 19:24:29 | refreshing | 211,253,549 | 27.7 s |
| 19:24:37 | committing | 3,514,856,529 | 36.6 s |
| 19:24:39 | logical_verification | 3,514,856,529 | 37.6 s |
| 19:24:40 | published | — | 39.5 s |
| 19:24:50 | next request, discovering | 0 | — |

Next cycle starts 9–10 s after publication, so maintenance is effectively continuous while the journals are live. `processed_sessions` is 3–4 per cycle; every cycle publishes.

**The live journals are read, repeatedly.** `lsof -p <daemon>` sampled every 400 ms for ~80 s during a cycle lists only those four Codex journals, 129 open observations in total. That matches the 210–312 MB of `processed_bytes` per cycle: the append is a few KB, the read is the whole journal, more than once.

**Disk is not the problem.** Publication reuses the previous segments through APFS `fclonefileat` (consecutive generations share 50 of 60 segment ids, and unchanged artifacts keep their certified digests). `du` reports the two generations separately (`.ctx` went 20 GB → 29 GB during the loop) while the volume moved by 47 MB in the same window, so the cost is CPU and I/O, not space.

## Expected

Steady-state cost should scale with appended bytes, not with live journal size or with generation size. Concretely:

- an append should extend the certified suffix of that source instead of re-reading and re-validating the whole journal on every cycle (the #1119 / #1130 fix appears to cover “a new session appears while an old journal is being appended”, not “the appended journal itself is large and live” — the four files here were opened by the previous generation and are still appended);
- consecutive live appends should be coalesced into one publication with a quiet period, instead of publishing per detected change;
- publication itself should not requalify inherited artifacts on every cycle when the candidate reuses them by clone (this looks like it already holds: `certified_artifact` reuses the predecessor digest for cloned files, so the observed 30 s refresh is source-side).

A supported debounce or rate limit for automatic maintenance would also be enough for hosts like this one; #282 asked for the same behaviour when it was an admission-loop bug.

## Impact and current workaround

While two harnesses are active, the daemon holds one to two cores indefinitely, which makes the machine unusable for other work. My workaround is `ctx index mode manual` plus a launchd job that runs `ctx import --incremental --quiet` every 30 minutes: ~1.4 s CPU per run, at the cost of freshness.

title: Feature request: opt-in lexical storage profile (tool-output projection, positions, docstore compression) + size breakdown in status
body:
## Request

Give the lexical generation a **documented, opt-in storage profile** so a host can trade search features for size, and surface the size composition so users can see where the bytes go.

Concretely, four things:

1. **Search-projection content scope.** Choose what goes into `body_search`: messages and tool-call metadata only, or tool-output bodies capped at N KiB per event (today they are always projected in full). Stored Core records would stay complete, so `show`/`list` stay exact; only lexical reachability into large tool output changes.
2. **Index record option.** Allow `WithFreqs` instead of `WithFreqsAndPositions` for the position-heavy case, accepting that phrase queries stop working.
3. **Docstore compression profile.** Keep Lz4 as default, allow zstd (or just a higher level) opt-in.
4. **Size observability.** Report the generation's byte split (docstore / inverted terms / positions / postings / fast fields), and the projected body bytes per event type, in `ctx status --format json` or `ctx stats`. Right now `du ~/.ctx` says 20 GB, `ctx status` says `3.4 GiB processed`, and neither explains the 9.5 GiB generation.

## Measured baseline

Environment: macOS arm64, ctx 2.3.0 (`0e1b92ab…`), one data root, 2,100 sources / 1,692 sessions across Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, Pi, Cursor, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, Warp.

Active generation: **9.55 GiB, 292,828 documents, 75 segments**.

| Component | Bytes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `.store` (docstore, `core_record`, lz4) | 5.18 GiB | 54 % |
| `.term` | 2.46 GiB | 26 % |
| `.pos` | 1.47 GiB | 15 % |
| `.idx` | 0.38 GiB | 4 % |
| `.fast` / `.fieldnorm` / `.del` | 0.05 GiB | <1 % |

Projected body text over all 283,514 events (`ctx list events --limit 400000 --content text`):

| Event type | Events | Body bytes | Average |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `tool_output` | 82,142 | **1.98 GiB** | 25.2 KB |
| `tool_call` | 100,043 | 0.11 GiB | 1.1 KB |
| `message` | 40,540 | 0.10 GiB | 2.7 KB |
| `command_output` | 11,163 | 0.04 GiB | 3.6 KB |
| `summary` + `notice` | 49,625 | ≈0 | 0.1–0.2 KB |
| **Total** | **283,514** | **2.23 GiB** | 7.7 KB |

1,559 events carry more than 100 KB of body text; the largest is 13.1 MB.

Two ratios explain the rest:

- **Inverted index ≈ 2× body.** 4.35 GiB of `term + pos + idx` for 2.23 GiB of body. Positions dominate, and Chinese is the expensive case: `ScriptAwareTokenizer` emits dense-script characters one token at a time, each with a position, so CJK bodies cost far more `.pos`/`.idx` per byte than Latin text.
- **Stored record ≈ 3× body.** Sampling `tool_output` events: 49 KB body → 149 KB `core_record` (3.05×), 3.4 KB → 12.7 KB (3.71×), with a ~1–2 KB metadata floor. About 6.8 GiB of records compress to the 5.18 GiB docstore.

Control case: a scratch data root containing only Claude Code chat (4.19 MB body) produces a 13.7 MB generation — docstore 1.24×, positions 1.04×, terms 0.56×, i.e. 3.3× overall. The measured root is 4.3× precisely because tool outputs carry the structured payload that dominates the docstore.

So this is not “10 GB for plain text”: it is 2.2 GiB of body, of which 89 % is tool output, stored once as a JSON record (~3×) and indexed once with positions (~2×).

## Where this is hardcoded today

- `crates/ctx-history-index-generation/src/generation.rs` — `lexical_index_settings()`: `Compressor::Lz4`, 32 KiB blocks.
- `crates/ctx-history-index-format/src/schema.rs` — `body_search` uses `IndexRecordOption::WithFreqsAndPositions`.
- `crates/ctx-history-index-format/src/analyzer.rs` — `ScriptAwareTokenizer` (dense scripts → per-character tokens).
- Docstore stores the whole `core_record`, which is what makes `show`/`list` exact.

## Suggested shape (for discussion, not a demand)

- A data-root-scoped, manifest-recorded setting alongside `[indexing] mode`, e.g. `[indexing] profile = "balanced" | "compact"`, immutable for an existing root and requiring a documented rebuild (`ctx import --all`) to change.
- `compact` = tool-output projection capped (or excluded, with `--content-scope outputs` then reporting that no output bodies are searchable), `WithFreqs` instead of `WithFreqsAndPositions`, zstd docstore.
- Schema/settings differences are already part of generation identity, so a profile change fits the existing “new generation or rebuild” semantics rather than becoming mutable runtime config.

## Why it matters

- Size: a normal multi-harness history is ~10 GiB of physical index today, and `du` reports 19–20 GiB because the retained previous generation is an APFS clone of the active one (measurements in #1146).
- It also feeds back into #1146: publish cost scales with generation size, so a compact profile would reduce refresh CPU as well.
- Users cannot make this trade-off today at any granularity — the only lever is “index fewer providers”, which loses entire histories instead of losing large tool bodies.

## Non-goals

Not asking to change defaults, drop retained data, or make profiles mutable in place. Opt-in, documented, and reversible by rebuild.

## Reproduction notes

```bash
# component sizes
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, collections
root = os.path.expanduser("~/.ctx/search/lexical")
gen = json.load(open(os.path.join(root, "active-generation.json")))["active"]["directory"]
p = os.path.join(root, "index-generations", gen)
sizes = collections.Counter()
for f in os.listdir(p):
    sizes[os.path.splitext(f)[1] or "(none)"] += os.stat(os.path.join(p, f)).st_size
meta = json.load(open(os.path.join(p, "meta.json")))
docs = sum(int(s.get("max_doc", 0)) for s in meta["segments"])
print(gen, docs, {k: round(v / 2**30, 2) for k, v in sizes.most_common()})
PY

# body bytes per event type
ctx list events --limit 400000 --content text --format jsonl | python3 -c '
import json, sys, collections
tot, cnt = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
for line in sys.stdin:
    ev = json.loads(line).get("event") or {}
    t = ev.get("event_type") or "(none)"
    body = ev.get("text") or ""
    if not isinstance(body, str):
        continue
    tot[t] += len(body.encode()); cnt[t] += 1
for t, c in cnt.most_common():
    print(f"{t:16s} n={c:7d} {tot[t]/2**30:6.2f} GiB avg={tot[t]/c/1024:7.1f} KB")
'
```

Happy to test a prototype profile on this root (292 k documents, repeatable rebuild) and report measured savings for each of the three levers separately.

title: Follow-up: accepted-snapshot archive update plans and incremental transfers
body:
## Problem

The portable archive baseline works on CTX 2.3.0. Project/time preview and creator-supplied query provenance are implemented. Repeated project handovers still require full selected snapshots, an externally assembled exact predecessor map when a conversation grows, and coordination between preview/export operations that independently choose generations.

This is a focused follow-up to the incremental-export and round-trip goals in the closed [ctxrs/ctx#1036](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/issues/1036), not another proposal for portable archives or a report that unchanged restores duplicate history.

## Impact

An operator periodically moves selected projects from device A to B and back, sometimes offline. The agent should prepare only the authorized project history, preserve its original identity, explain what changed since the last accepted transfer, safely handle continued conversations, and produce deterministic evidence that the destination accepted the intended snapshot.

For repeated large snapshots, unchanged restores being logically idempotent does not eliminate the cost of exporting/transferring unchanged payloads. Conversely, making corrections easier must not weaken the existing exact-predecessor safeguard.

## Synthetic example

All device/account labels, conversation labels and revisions below are fictional; `r1`, `r2` and `r3` are symbolic revision labels, not actual digests.

| Situation | Intended plan/result |
|---|---|
| A exports Coral conversations C1 at r1 and C2 at r1 under stable `origin-a-1`/`personal`; B accepts the snapshot | Record B's accepted baseline and retain enough identity/digest evidence for another transfer |
| A extends C1 to r2 and adds C3 at r1; C2 is unchanged | Explain one changed, one unchanged and one new member; allow efficient transfer of only required new/changed payloads |
| B still has the accepted C1 r1 | Authorize the reviewed C1 r1-to-r2 correction from the accepted baseline, without manually reconstructing a hash map |
| B already accepted C1 r3 through another transfer | Reject the stale predecessor; do not overwrite r3 merely because the incoming archive says r2 is desired |
| B creates an independent native conversation D1 | Return D1 under `origin-b-1`; preserve A's identity when forwarding any of A's original members |
| The source changes after a preview, or the requested selection is empty | Execute the exact approved selection or reject/re-plan; never silently export a newer/wider selection or fall back to all history |

One possible interface is a reviewable transfer/update plan plus an acceptance receipt; an improved existing snapshot/inventory workflow could also satisfy the need. Exact CLI names, formats, container layout, transport and implementation belong to the maintainer, and the outcomes can be delivered in stages.

## Desired behavior and acceptance criteria

- Bind reviewed work to the explicit origin/view, project/workspace and optional time bounds, source generation, selected portable member identities, payload digests and accepted destination baseline. Clearly distinguish new, unchanged and changed members.
- Supply complete machine-readable selection/scope evidence, or explicit incompleteness. A bounded/truncated human preview alone is insufficient for a checker to authorize unseen members; a paginated or saved review artifact is acceptable.
- Execute the reviewed immutable selection, or reject it as stale and require a new review. Do not silently change generation, widen project scope or freeze/disable unrelated native capture to make the workflow work.
- Preserve whole-conversation semantics and expose out-of-window, mixed/unknown-workspace and other scope warnings. Do not imply event-level redaction or semantic privacy classification; ambiguous selections still need explicit review.
- Derive changed-member authorization from an explicitly chosen previously accepted snapshot/inventory and compare with the destination's actual current predecessor. The incoming revision is not its own overwrite authority.
- Support skipping unchanged payload transfer, with explicit base-snapshot dependencies and verification of required base members. Retain the option of a full independently restorable snapshot.
- Preserve stable origin/member identities through A-to-B-to-A forwarding. Unchanged repeats remain no-ops; unrelated accounts/origins remain distinct even if provider session IDs or content coincide.
- Verify incoming content and dependencies before atomic publication. Corrupt/incomplete archives, incompatible formats or predecessor conflicts must leave the previous searchable destination state usable and report the rejected transfer explicitly.
- Produce a machine-readable acceptance receipt binding the accepted snapshot/digests, member outcomes and resulting searchable generation, with enough evidence to check arrival without interpreting ranked hit counts or copying transcript bodies into logs.
- Keep restore additive unless a separate destructive operation is explicitly requested. Do not introduce implicit pruning, raw shared writable native roots, automatic account enrollment or mandatory online synchronization.

## Validation and related work

The baseline was independently exercised on CTX 2.3.0 at public upstream commit `0e1b92ab6`, without product patches. Unchanged restores and origin-preserving forwarding were no-ops; a changed member conflicted while old history remained searchable; supplying the exact accepted predecessors permitted the correction. These safeguards are working and should be reused, not replaced with unconditional overwrite.

Workspace/time selection and preview already shipped in [ctxrs/ctx#1138](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/pull/1138), and provenance in [ctxrs/ctx#1134](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/pull/1134). The remaining request is accepted-baseline update ergonomics and incremental transport from [ctxrs/ctx#1036](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/issues/1036). Native provider-file backup, harness resumption, built-in encryption, repository synchronization and hosted-service deployment are outside this follow-up.

title: Feature request: explicit project context views across native, imported and shared history
body:
## Problem

CTX 2.3.0 provides working normalized archive transfer, archive provenance and scoped hosted sharing. However, an agent must separately choose ordinary native search, an archive-owned history root, or a saved server connection. Moving a project repository does not tell its next agent which retained history to consult, and a successful local search can overlook earlier decisions that are already available elsewhere.

The same project can have different recorded workspace paths on different devices/accounts. Using only the current checkout's path is therefore insufficient even after choosing the correct history surface.

## Impact

The intended operator instruction is "prepare this project on the other device" rather than a list of history roots, origin labels, workspace aliases and connection flags. An agent should be able to inspect one explicit project context definition, discover which authorized sources are available, retrieve the retained decisions and tool results, and report when coverage is partial.

Manual query routing is a workable fallback today. The improvement is a supported retrieval contract that survives project handovers, not automatic publication, a merged writable index, or removal of account boundaries.

## Synthetic example

All labels and examples below are fictional; variables stand for operator-configured bindings, not actual filesystem paths or credentials.

| Step | Available history | What the next agent needs |
|---|---|---|
| Work on project Coral on device A | Native account history associated with `WORKSPACE_A` | Retain a design decision and its tool result |
| Move Coral to device B | A's verified archive is in an archive-owned root; new B sessions enter B's native root under `WORKSPACE_B` | Find both the earlier decision and current work without confusing the two origins |
| A second account contributes to Coral | The separately enrolled account publishes to an authorized shared collection | Query that contribution without sharing either account's private index directory |
| Work offline on B | Native and imported history remain available; the shared connection is unavailable | Return useful available context with an explicit incomplete-source report, not a misleading complete success |
| Return to A | Context bindings resolve to A's paths/connections | Reuse the project intent without copying B's credentials or guessing workspace aliases |

Today the agent has to orchestrate separate supported queries, for example:

```sh
ctx search "coral decision marker" --workspace "$WORKSPACE_B" --refresh off
ctx --data-root "$IMPORTED_HISTORY" search "coral decision marker" \
  --workspace "$WORKSPACE_A" --refresh off
ctx --server "$SHARED_CONNECTION" search "coral decision marker"
```

The desired outcome is one explicitly selected project context entry point covering these permitted surfaces. A named view, a project context manifest, or another interface could provide that; these examples do not prescribe command names, configuration format, storage layout or a query engine.

## Desired behavior and acceptance criteria

- Allow an explicitly chosen project context to bind permitted native/archive roots and saved shared connections, with declared recorded-workspace aliases for each source. Preserve ordinary local-only search.
- Provide machine-readable, read-only inspection of effective sources, project filters and availability/access state, without exposing credentials. A missing binding must be reported rather than silently omitted or initialized as a new native capture root.
- Query the configured sources and explicitly distinguish complete, partial, offline, forbidden and failed-source outcomes. Respect existing refresh controls; do not hide an unavailable shared source behind successful local results.
- Label results with their query surface, origin and provenance authority. Distinguish creator-asserted archive labels from authenticated shared publisher/collection evidence.
- Preserve usable follow-up references for full retained conversations, individual events and structured tool activity. Opaque shared citations must remain routable to the correct backend instead of being mistaken for local IDs.
- If the same portable contribution/revision is reachable through more than one surface, handle it using proven identity or label the alternatives. Never merge unrelated origins just because text or provider session IDs coincide, and do not present retained old revisions as multiple current conversations.
- Define session-level versus event-level result handling and bounded-query/partial-coverage semantics so agents do not use raw hit totals as completeness evidence.
- Let a project context definition travel with a project while endpoint-local paths/connections are resolved explicitly; credentials and account enrollment remain private and separate.
- Selecting or inspecting a context must not publish, enroll accounts, widen audiences, enable semantic processing, change the global capture root or alter native discovery. Existing permissions remain authoritative.

## Validation and scope

The baseline was independently exercised on CTX 2.3.0 at public upstream commit `0e1b92ab6`, without product patches: physical archive round trips, two-way account publication, scoped future capture, retained tool activity, stable-origin no-op restores and local archive provenance worked. The missing ergonomics are combined retrieval and explicit project context discovery, not those transport/integrity features.

This request assumes already-supported providers and separately authorized source access. Native harness resumption, fleet-wide capture policy, repository-file synchronization, credential distribution and automatic private-topic classification are outside its scope.
