title: Bound lexical rebuild memory, staging merges, worker concurrency, and generation retention
body:
Fixes #1192

### Summary
- Add configurable `indexing.memory_mb` and `indexing.workers` limits coordinated across Tantivy indexing, merge threads, and parallel leaf scanners so constrained hosts stay within their memory and CPU budget instead of stalling or OOMing during large rebuilds.
- Add an anonymous spill-backed changed-session registry (`ChangedSessionRegistry`) so lowering `indexing.memory_mb` (down to 15 MiB) runs within memory bounds instead of aborting large multi-ten-thousand-session rebuilds, while preserving non-retryable `ResourceUnavailable` (`IndexMemoryLimit`) classification across serial and parallel route scans if the safety ceiling is hit.
- Replace unbounded deferred staging merges with `StagingLexicalMergePolicy` (bounded segment ceiling with incremental fan-in compaction, bounded merge thread count, and quiesced rollback/discard handling).
- Retire an unleased `previous` generation directory before starting an upgrade or rebuild-marked full rebuild so large upgrades do not keep three full copies on disk, while protecting active generations, leased `previous` slots, and flat-delta base manifests.
- Surface read-only `lexical.upgrade` scope, progress, and ETA in `ctx status` during schema/settings upgrades (excluding physical checksum corruption) and preserve whole-run ETA when full-scope `ctx import --all` coalesces onto an active rebuild.

### Validation
- Passed `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run` across all affected index, capture, refresh, daemon, and presentation crates, and `ctx-history-index` doctests.
- Passed repository policy, public docs, public control surface, LOC, and Rust crate-size gates.

title: Treat rebuild-required predecessor generations as fresh rebuilds with metadata continuity
body:
Fixes #1178

### Summary
- Classify readable predecessor generations that require a full schema rebuild (such as schema 22 -> 23 upgrades or active rebuild markers) as rebuild-required rather than writable base snapshots so upgrades never fail with "retired route was not carried".
- Separate reusable Tantivy write base (`reusable_write_base`) from readable predecessor continuity (`readable_predecessor`) so schema 22 -> 23 rebuilds still preserve manifest-stored explicit sources (`--path` / `--custom-jsonl`) and `Released` / detached configured provider-root authorities.
- Prevent silent provider or route loss during rebuilds by widening scoped CLI imports (`--provider`, `--path`) to a complete catalog rebuild while requiring executable routes for `--provider`, suppressing startup Hermes exact reconciliation and paused-route `Exact` fallbacks while a rebuild is pending, rejecting `Exact` publication scope against rebuild-required generations at execution time, and allowing widened scoped imports to recover cleanly if a crash happens right after `active-generation.json` advances to schema 23.

### Validation
- Passed `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run` across `ctx-history-index`, `ctx-history-capture-composition`, `ctx-history-refresh-execution`, `ctx-history-refresh`, and `ctx --test offline_default -E "test(schema_upgrade)"`.
- Passed repository policy, public docs, public control surface, LOC, and Rust crate-size gates.

title: Add authenticated manifest summary sidecar for zero-manifest-read query opens
body:
Fixes #1181

### Summary
- Write and verify a compact `<generation_id>.summary.json` sidecar alongside full, exact-reuse, and flat-delta generation manifests, carrying certified source totals, archive source count, bounded present non-empty route identities, and flat-delta `base_generation_id`.
- Cryptographically bind the sidecar digest (`summary_sha256`) into `GenerationSlot` (`active-generation.json`, optional for backward compatibility with existing `2.3.0`/`2.4.0`/`2.4.1` pointers) so tampered sidecars are rejected and query opens trust the sidecar only when its SHA-256 matches the active pointer.
- Resolve flat-delta `base_generation_id` during read-lease acquisition from the authenticated summary without reading or hashing the full flat-delta manifest, while metering fallback reads through `read_metrics`.
- Replace infallible `VerifiedIndex::manifest()` with fallible `try_manifest()` and `into_generation_snapshot() -> Result<...>` across the workspace so corrupt or unreadable full manifests behind lazy query readers return typed `IndexError` values instead of panicking.
- Eliminate full-manifest reads from read-only `ctx search`, archive provenance checks when no archive sources exist, and inline `Published` refresh receipts.

### Validation
- Passed `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (all 80 crates), `cargo nextest run` across index, format, generation, query, archive, refresh, CLI, and schema-upgrade suites, plus doctests.
- Passed repository policy, public docs, public control surface, LOC, and Rust crate-size gates.

title: fix(daemon): prevent the Windows logon task from opening a terminal
body:
On Windows, starting the managed daemon can open a Terminal window that stays on screen for as long as the daemon runs. The logon task starts PowerShell with `-WindowStyle Hidden`. Windows can open the console before PowerShell reads that option. [Windows Terminal report](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/12464) · [Console startup discussion](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/249)

The task now starts a small Rust executable built for the Windows GUI subsystem. It starts the existing PowerShell supervisor with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, waits for it, and returns its exit code to Task Scheduler. A Windows job object ensures that ending the task also stops PowerShell. When ctx repairs an existing registration, it installs the launcher beside the task definition and replaces the old action. [Windows process creation flags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-creation-flags)

The launcher ships inside `ctx.exe`. Bazel builds it as a Rust binary. For stable Cargo, the runtime’s build script compiles the launcher for the requested Windows target in its own build directory. The runtime embeds that executable with `include_bytes!`. The launcher uses the workspace’s existing `windows-sys` dependency. We could also remove the nested build and use the Cargo nightly artifact dependency (`artifact = "bin"`, `target = "target"`) if you would prefer. [Cargo artifact dependencies (`-Z bindeps`)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/unstable.html#artifact-dependencies)

title: Reclaim superseded payloads from archive-owned roots
body:
### Reproduce

With ctx 2.5.0, restore a portable archive into an archive-owned root. Append an event to the original conversation, export it again, and restore the new archive with the exact predecessor digest. Repeating that update leaves each revision's full original payload under `archives/`. Search and a fresh export correctly use the latest indexed revision.

### Requested behavior

Add a supported way to reclaim superseded payloads in an archive-owned root. An active export can pin an older generation and then resolve its original members. Cleanup must preserve every object referenced by the active, recovery or still-pinned generation and coordinate with restore. A preview and a machine-readable receipt would show which verified objects are eligible and how many bytes apply reclaimed.

For qualification, a synthetic root can have one growing conversation and a distinct retained view. Verify the active export before and after cleanup, preserve the retained view and a pinned predecessor, and exercise an interrupted or repeated cleanup.

title: Prune verified superseded archive payloads
body:
Closes #1220.

Adds `ctx archive prune` for archive-owned roots. Preview is the default and `--apply` reclaims verified superseded copies. The command uses the restore lock, protects active and recovery generations, and defers while an older generation has a reader. Each candidate must be covered record for record by its current original view. Interrupted removals resume from the owned staging directory.

Linux qualification:
- `cargo test --locked -p ctx-history-archive --lib` passed 31 tests. One existing large-history test remained ignored.
- The release CLI was built with Rust 1.97.1. On a synthetic root created by ctx 2.4.1, preview found one eligible snapshot and changed no payloads. Apply reclaimed one snapshot and 4,912 bytes. A repeated apply reclaimed zero. Both original views had byte-identical inventories on re-export.

title: 2.5.0 upgrade: full semantic re-embed holds Core refresh for hours; status reports "waiting for admission"
body:
# After upgrading to 2.5.0, Core refresh is starved for hours behind the semantic re-embed, and status reports it as "waiting for admission"

## Summary

After upgrading 2.3.0 → 2.5.0 with automatic indexing and built-in semantic search enabled, the daemon published one Core generation shortly after start and then published nothing for hours. New transcript writes were not indexed. A `ctx search --refresh wait` request sat in `admission_pending` with 0 bytes processed for over 20 minutes and is still there.

The cause is not admission. The daemon scheduler gives semantic catch-up for the published generation priority over both dirty-route refresh and an already queued Core request. The upgrade changed the semantic source contract fingerprint, so every source is re-embedded without vector reuse. On this corpus that re-embed runs for roughly five hours, and Core freshness waits for all of it.

`ctx status` and `ctx doctor` say only `History work  waiting for admission; search request` / `refresh is pending (core_refresh_pending)`. Nothing points at semantic catch-up.

## Environment

- ctx 2.5.0 (managed install, tag commit 0b117cb), upgraded from 2.3.0
- macOS 26.x, Apple Silicon, 14 CPUs, 24 GiB RAM, heavy swap in use
- indexing `auto`, daemon mode `full`, semantic enabled, built-in executor (CoreML), `builtin_throttling` default (true)
- Corpus: about 4,000 sources, 933,132 indexed documents, 11 GB lexical index, about 22,400 semantic documents / 89,900 chunks

## Timeline (local time)

- 10:05 binary replaced; 10:06 daemon started.
- 10:09 last Core publication (generation `374f6d75…`). No Core refresh has run since.
- 11:13 first semantic segment written under the new source contract fingerprint (`17b7fe9d…`). Everything before that used `6c5d22aa…`. Between 10:09 and 11:13 there were almost no semantic writes, and I have not determined what the daemon was doing.
- 12:30 `ctx search --refresh wait` submits a Core refresh. `jobs/core-refresh.json`: `request_state: admission_pending`, `logical_phase: waiting`, `trigger: search`, progress all zero.
- 12:54 still `admission_pending`. Semantic job: `status: budget_exhausted`, `source_generation_ready: false`, `source_work_remaining: true`, `semantic_progress_sequence` climbing about 1–9 per minute.

## What the state shows

Semantic frontier (`semantic_maintenance_state.core_semantic_frontier_v1`, read from a copy of `search/semantic/state.sqlite`):

- `source_traversal_phase: reconciling_sources`
- `source_traversal_after_identity_digest: 513c6dd9…` at 12:53:56. Sources are traversed in digest order, so this is about 32% through the digest space after about 100 minutes since 11:13.
- `vector_reuse_allowed: false`

Flat source receipts across `flat_segments/flat-catalog-*.json`, latest receipt per source:

| contract fingerprint | sources | indexed documents | semantic-eligible documents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `17b7fe9d…` (2.5.0) | 1,287 | 299,374 | 6,978 |
| `6c5d22aa…` (pre-upgrade) | 2,708 | 604,782 | 15,425 |

At the observed rate, the remaining 67% takes about 3.5 more hours. Core refresh stays blocked for that whole time.

A 3-second `sample` of the daemon showed the main thread in `read()` in 2,543 of 2,576 samples, in the semantic code region. The process used about 1.7% CPU, so this pass looks I/O-bound rather than inference-bound. Symbols are stripped, so I cannot name the function.

## Mechanism (v2.5.0)

- Pending Core request plus a semantic turn pending: the scheduler runs one semantic durable boundary and returns, before it reaches `run_core_refresh`. [`daemon_scheduler.rs#L113-L144`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-daemon-service/src/daemon_scheduler.rs#L113-L144)
- The turn stays pending while the job reports `budget_exhausted` with `source_generation_ready == false` and `source_work_remaining == true`. [`semantic_fairness.rs#L16-L30`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-daemon-service/src/daemon_scheduler/semantic_fairness.rs#L16-L30) That is true for every boundary of a full re-embed.
- Admission of the queued request is resolved only inside `CoreRefreshEngine::run_next`. [`resolution.rs#L4-L34`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-history-refresh/src/engine/request_lifecycle/resolution.rs#L4-L34) Because the scheduler never calls it, the request reports `admission_pending` indefinitely.
- With no queued request, semantic `Drain` catch-up runs first and returns early whenever it did a turn. Dirty-route Core refresh is reached only after semantic has nothing left to do. [`daemon_scheduler.rs#L179-L218`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-daemon-service/src/daemon_scheduler.rs#L179-L218) That explains why filesystem-driven refresh also stopped at 10:09.
- Vector reuse requires a matching contract fingerprint or a trusted legacy fingerprint. [`state.rs#L66-L74`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-semantic-index/src/vector_store/source_projection/state.rs#L66-L74) The pre-upgrade receipts did not qualify, so every source is re-embedded.
- This ordering is intended: [`daemon-semantic-indexing-spec.md#L25-L30`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/docs/daemon-semantic-indexing-spec.md#L25-L30) and the test `queued_core_successor_waits_for_semantic_readiness_across_restart` ([`daemon_scheduler_tests.rs#L786-L933`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-daemon-service/src/daemon_scheduler_tests.rs#L786-L933)). The stated reason is to stop continuously changing Core generations from restarting semantic work forever. That reason holds for incremental catch-up that finishes in seconds or minutes. It does not hold for a corpus-wide re-embed after an upgrade, where the cost is hours of stale history.

## Expected

After an upgrade, new history becomes searchable lexically within the normal refresh cadence, even while the semantic projection is being rebuilt.

## Asks

1. **Bound how long semantic can hold Core.** When the semantic pass for a generation is a full re-embed, for example `vector_reuse_allowed == false` across the traversal, or after a wall-clock or boundary budget, let a queued or dirty Core refresh run between semantic turns. Pick whichever fits the design: interleave one Core cycle per N semantic boundaries, or skip the readiness wait when the pass cannot finish soon.
2. **Report the real wait.** When a Core request is held because a semantic turn is pending, `ctx status` / `ctx doctor` should say so, for example "Core refresh waits for semantic catch-up (32% of sources)", instead of "waiting for admission". Today the only way to find the cause is to read the scheduler source.
3. **Carry legacy receipts across contract bumps** when the change does not affect vectors, or document in the release notes that the upgrade re-embeds every source and holds Core refresh until that finishes, with a rough cost per source.
4. Optional: report semantic traversal progress (sources done/total) in `ctx semantic status`. Right now only `semantic_progress_sequence` is visible, and it has no denominator.

## Workarounds considered

- Waiting works. Core resumes when the semantic pass reaches `ready`.
- `[semantic] builtin_throttling = false` removes inter-batch pacing. The pass looks I/O-bound here, so the gain may be small. I have not measured it.
- `ctx semantic disable` would unblock Core, because the catch-up then returns no turn. Its effect on the partly rebuilt projection is not documented, so I have not tried it.

## Related

- #860 (closed by #866): semantic hard-fails after every Core generation. Fixed with the fairness turns that cause this starvation.
- #1192 (closed): lexical generation upgrade memory bound. 2.5.0 added `indexing.memory_mb` / `indexing.workers`. Those settings do not apply here, because nothing is admitted.
- #1182 (open): shallow revalidation of grown append-only sources.

title: OpenCode `idle` and `location-switched` rows are rejected as unsupported record types
body:
## Summary

OpenCode 2.x writes two lifecycle message types to `session_message` that ctx's native OpenCode adapter rejects as an unsupported record type: `idle` and `location-switched`. Neither holds conversation content, but every one is counted as a rejected record, so a healthy OpenCode store never reports complete coverage and the rejected count grows by about one per turn.

## Environment

- ctx 2.5.0 (also seen on 2.4.1)
- OpenCode 2.3.2 and 2.4.1, native SQLite store (`opencode.db`)
- Linux x86_64

## Steps

1. Use OpenCode 2.x for a while (every completed turn writes an `idle` row; changing a session's directory writes `location-switched`).
2. Let ctx index the native OpenCode store.
3. `ctx status --format json`

## Actual

`refresh.current.current_rejected_records` is non-zero and `refresh.diagnostics.record_rejections` lists rows like:

```json
{"provider": "opencode", "detail": "OpenCode SQLite row has an unsupported record type", "line": 123456}
```

On one store: 2,209 rejected rows, all `session_message.type` values `idle` (2,194) or `location-switched` (15). `rejection_diagnostics_shown: 64`, `omitted: 2145`.

The rows contain only lifecycle metadata, for example:

- `idle`: `{"time": {...}, "outcome": "succeeded"}`
- `location-switched`: the previous and new directory and project ID

All other message types in the same store (`user`, `assistant`, `system`, `synthetic`, `compaction`, `agent-switched`, `model-switched`) are accepted, and searching finds the conversations.

## Expected

`idle` and `location-switched` are ignored or kept as notice events rather than rejected, the same way #815 resolved OpenCode file parts, so a store with only these rows reports no rejected records.

## Notes

- These types are not new in 2.4.x: one store has had `idle` rows since 2026-10-01 and `location-switched` since 2026-10-14.
- In 2.4.1 and 2.5.0, neither type appears in the OpenCode adapter's accepted message types (around `native_path_json_output.rs:60`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Indexing an OpenCode store whose only otherwise-unhandled rows are `idle` and `location-switched` reports `current_rejected_records: 0`.
- Conversation content and search results for that store are unchanged.

title: Hybrid search takes ~15 s per query: fast-field columns reopened per document in semantic_filter_projection, plus a full flat-F32 reload
body:
## Observation

On 2.5.0 (managed install, Linux/WSL2, 24 cores, 62 GB RAM, auto indexing, built-in semantic on CUDA), a hybrid `ctx search` takes 14.5-16.3 s and peaks at about 3.1 GB RSS while `ctx semantic status` reports `ready`. The same query with `--backend lexical` finishes in 0.1-0.8 s at 220 MB.

| Command | Wall | User CPU | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctx search "<q>" --refresh off --limit 8` (hybrid) | 14.5-16.3 s | 12.0-13.1 s | 3.1 GB |
| same, `--backend lexical` | 0.1-0.8 s | 0.1-0.5 s | 220 MB |
| 4 hybrid searches started together | 63.5 s each | | 3.1 GB each (~12.4 GB total) |

Parallel searches share no work, so four at once finish in 63.8 s against about 72 s run back to back. Agent harnesses often run several history searches at once, and each pays the full cost. #619 and #1069 reported per-search memory and parallel contention earlier; lexical search has since dropped to 220 MB, and the remaining cost is in the semantic path.

## Profile

I built `0b117cba` with `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only` and sampled one hybrid search under gdb every 250 ms (56 busy samples):

| Samples | Where |
|---|---|
| 31 | `semantic_filter_projection` → `core_event_identity_fast_preflight` → `core_document_fast_facts` → `unique_fast_u64` (`stored_document.rs:52`), inside Tantivy column deserialization |
| ~15 | flat-F32 store load: `load_pinned_generation` → `load_and_validate_segment` → `map_artifact_in_directory` (SHA-256, `open`, `mmap`, `statx`) |
| the rest | manifest/catalog decoding and `validate_manifest` |

## Cause 1: fast-field columns reopened for every document

`semantic_filter_projection` (`ctx-history-index-query/src/execution/search/semantic_projection.rs`) collects every document matching `event_type=message AND role=user` under the search filter. With no filter that is every user message in the index, about 87K here. For each one it calls `core_event_identity_fast_preflight`, which opens five fast-field columns from the segment reader (`event_id_high`, `event_id_low`, `core_record_encoded_bytes`, `core_content_bytes` through `unique_fast_u64`, and the `event_range_order` bytes column), reads one value from each, and drops them. That is roughly 435K column opens per search, and each open deserializes the column's codec metadata. The projection only uses the event ID and the identity digest.

## Cause 2: quadratic snapshot check in `validate_manifest`

For each source snapshot, `validate_manifest` (`ctx-semantic-index/src/vector_store/flat_segments/validation.rs:333`) checks for a matching base segment with `manifest.segments.iter().any(...)`. With 14,273 snapshots and 40,546 segments that is up to ~579M comparisons on every pin.

## Fix

#1225 fixes both. Behavior and error cases are unchanged.

- `ctx-history-index-format`: add `CoreDocumentFastFactColumns`, which opens the four `u64` columns once per segment and returns `CoreDocumentFastFacts` for a doc with the same validation. `core_document_fast_facts` now delegates to it.
- `ctx-history-index-query`: add `CoreEventIdentityColumns` (those columns plus the `event_range_order` bytes column) and replace `core_event_identity_fast_preflight`, whose only caller was the projection. `semantic_filter_projection` sorts the matched addresses and opens columns once per segment.
- `validate_manifest`: build a `HashSet` of `(generation, source_identity_digest)` for base segments once and look each snapshot up in it.

Results on the same store, alternating the stock 2.5.0 binary and the patched build, ready-state runs only:

| | Wall | User CPU |
|---|---|---|
| stock 2.5.0 | 14.5-16.3 s | 12.0-13.1 s |
| patched | 6.0-11.0 s | 3.7-3.9 s |

Wall time varies with disk I/O while the daemon is active. Ranks, event IDs, and `retrieval_score` were identical between the two builds for all four queries I compared. `cargo test` passes for `ctx-history-index-format`, `ctx-history-index-query`, and `ctx-semantic-index`; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean for all three.

## What remains: the flat-F32 store is rebuilt on every query

After the fix, most of the remaining time is loading the flat store, and peak memory stays at ~3.1 GB because of it. `load_pinned_generation` (`flat_segments/pinned.rs:198`) runs `load_and_validate_segment` on every descriptor, and `map_artifact_in_directory` stats, opens, mmaps, and SHA-256s every vectors, metadata, and mutations file. `strace -c` for one search:

```text
statx     281,925 calls
openat    140,983
mmap      138,561
munmap    138,417
close     141,191
```

A standalone script doing the same stat/open/mmap/SHA-256 pass over the store takes about 4 s. The pinned generation is cached only inside one process for one flat generation (`load_pinned`), and each search is a new process, so it always reloads.

Store state at the time (`search/semantic/flat_segments`, 3.0 GiB, 121,928 files; corpus of 14,273 sources, 3.53M documents, 454K active chunks):

- 40,546 segment descriptors (18,589 base, 21,955 delta), three files each
- 12,993 base segments with zero vectors, 2,299 of them under `flat-unscoped-source`
- 1,452,785 stored vectors for 453,762 active chunks, so about two-thirds of what each query loads is superseded
- every non-unscoped base segment has a generation from 20523 (written 2026-09-29) onward, so no full compaction has completed since then

Full compaction (`compact_coordinated`) writes one segment per source group, including sources with no events, so the floor here is 14,273 segments. Per-source compaction triggers at 16 segments for a source, which almost none reach. The stored > 2x active check in `compact_if_needed` only runs after replacement publishes and returns early during reconciliation. The unconditional compaction at the end of a reconciliation should clear the dead data, but it has not run here in eight weeks; `ctx semantic status` reports `source_work_remaining: true`. I haven't confirmed why. #1222 shows semantic source work running for hours on 2.5.0, which may be related.

Possible directions, which I haven't implemented:

- Verify payload checksums when a segment is written or compacted and check only headers and lengths on query.
- Let the daemon hold the pinned generation across CLI and MCP queries.
- Merge small segments across sources instead of keeping one per source, and drop zero-vector bases, including the unscoped ones.
- Run the stored > 2x active check on the source-backed refresh path.

## Reproduction

There is no small synthetic repro because the cost scales with the number of user messages and segments. On any large auto-indexed corpus, with standard Linux tools (`/usr/bin/time` is GNU time, from the `time` package; `strace` is its own package):

```bash
# confirm semantic search is ready
ctx semantic status

# hybrid vs lexical: wall seconds, user CPU seconds, peak RSS in KB
/usr/bin/time -f "%e s %U user %M KB" ctx search "anything" --refresh off --limit 5 --format json >/dev/null
/usr/bin/time -f "%e s %U user %M KB" ctx search "anything" --backend lexical --refresh off --limit 5 --format json >/dev/null

# number of flat segment files on disk
find ~/.ctx/search/semantic/flat_segments -type f | wc -l

# syscall totals for one hybrid search
strace -f -c -o /tmp/ctx-search.strace ctx search "anything" --refresh off --limit 5 --format json >/dev/null
head -n 12 /tmp/ctx-search.strace
```

If `ctx semantic status` is not `ready`, the search falls back to lexical and returns quickly, so check it right before timing. On macOS, `/usr/bin/time -l` gives wall time and peak memory, and `ls ~/.ctx/search/semantic/flat_segments | wc -l` gives the file count.

Related: #619, #1069, #1222.

title: Open semantic projection fast-field columns once per segment
body:
Fixes part of #1224.

## Summary

- open the semantic projection's fast-field columns once per segment instead of once per matched document
- check manifest source snapshots against a set of base segments instead of scanning every segment per snapshot
- no change to results, validation, or error cases

## Why

`semantic_filter_projection` resolves every document matching `event_type=message AND role=user` through `core_event_identity_fast_preflight`. That function opened five fast-field columns per document (`event_id_high`, `event_id_low`, `core_record_encoded_bytes`, `core_content_bytes`, and the `event_range_order` bytes column), read one value from each, and dropped them. With no filter that runs for every user message in the index. On the corpus in #1224 (~87K user messages) that is ~435K column opens per hybrid search, and gdb sampling of a symbolized build put 31 of 56 busy samples inside that path.

`CoreDocumentFastFactColumns` (format crate) and `CoreEventIdentityColumns` (query crate) hold the columns for one segment and apply the same per-document checks as before. `core_document_fast_facts` delegates to the new type, and `core_event_identity_fast_preflight` is replaced, since the projection was its only caller. The projection sorts the matched addresses and reopens columns only when the segment changes.

`validate_manifest` checked each source snapshot with `manifest.segments.iter().any(...)`, which is quadratic: 14,273 snapshots against 40,546 segments on that store. It now builds the `(generation, source_identity_digest)` set for base segments once.

## Results

Same store, alternating the stock 2.5.0 binary and this branch, ready-state hybrid searches with `--refresh off`:

| | Wall | User CPU |
|---|---|---|
| stock 2.5.0 | 14.5-16.3 s | 12.0-13.1 s |
| this branch | 6.0-11.0 s | 3.7-3.9 s |

Ranks, event IDs, and `retrieval_score` were identical for all four queries compared. Wall time varies with disk I/O from the running daemon. Most of what remains is the per-query flat-F32 reload described in #1224, which this PR does not change.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p ctx-history-index-format -p ctx-history-index-query -p ctx-semantic-index`
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the same three crates
- no new files or dependencies; I have not run the Bazel build locally

title: Pi discovery fails the whole route when OMP copies a subagent transcript into a continued session
body:
## Observation

On 2.5.0, a configured Pi root pointing at an OMP sessions directory (`ctx sources add omp --provider pi --root ~/.omp/agent/sessions`) indexes nothing. Every refresh and `ctx import --provider pi` fails the whole route:

```text
source-backed refresh retained no usable source: source-backed scan failed for pi at <root>:
invalid_source (invalid capture payload): invalid capture payload: Pi inventory repeats a native session identity
```

`ctx status` shows the root as included and reports the refresh as partial, while `ctx sessions --provider pi` stays empty.

## Cause

OMP keeps a session's subagent transcripts in a folder next to the session file (`<session>/<Agent>.jsonl`). When a session is continued or forked, OMP copies those transcripts into the new session's folder, and the copies keep the original `session` header, so the same native session ID appears at more than one path.

Pi discovery (`ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed/discovery.rs:216-224`) keys each file by the source derived from its header. The first time a second file with that source has a different observation, it returns `CaptureError::InvalidPayload("Pi inventory repeats a native session identity")` for the whole inventory, so one copied transcript removes every Pi session from the route.

Claude discovery already contains this case per member: conflicting transcripts are rejected with `with_quarantined_source`, one deterministic member carries the diagnostic, and the rest of the route publishes.

On my OMP store the copies were never conflicting. There were 79 repeated identities across 236 files: 75 groups were byte-identical copies, and in the other 4 each shorter copy was an exact byte prefix of the longest one (the original stopped growing when the session was continued). The whole Pi root, about 2,900 sessions, was excluded because of them.

## Reproduction

Standard shell tools only; uses a temporary data root and leaves nothing behind.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
W="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
P="$W/sessions/-tmp-proj"
mkdir -p "$P/2026-11-16T00-00-00-000Z_parent" "$P/2026-11-16T01-00-00-000Z_continued" "$W/ctx"

transcript() {
  printf '%s\n' '{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"01a01e7d-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","timestamp":"2026-11-16T00:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/tmp/proj"}'
  printf '%s\n' '{"type":"message","id":"00000001","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-11-16T00:00:01.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"first"}],"timestamp":1794787201000}}'
}
transcript > "$P/2026-11-16T00-00-00-000Z_parent/Researcher.jsonl"
cp "$P/2026-11-16T00-00-00-000Z_parent/Researcher.jsonl" "$P/2026-11-16T01-00-00-000Z_continued/Researcher.jsonl"

# An unrelated session in the same root.
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"01a01e7d-0000-7000-8000-000000000002","timestamp":"2026-11-16T02:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/tmp/proj"}' \
  '{"type":"message","id":"00000002","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-11-16T02:00:01.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"other"}],"timestamp":1794794401000}}' \
  > "$P/2026-11-16T02-00-00-000Z_other.jsonl"

export CTX_DATA_ROOT="$W/ctx" CTX_DAEMON_ENABLED=false
ctx index mode manual >/dev/null
ctx sources add omp --provider pi --root "$W/sessions" >/dev/null
ctx import --provider pi --no-blame --progress none
ctx sessions --provider pi
```

On 2.5.0 the import fails with `Pi inventory repeats a native session identity` and the unrelated session is not indexed either. With the fix in #1227, the import completes and both sessions are listed.

title: Resolve repeated Pi native session identities per member
body:
Fixes #1226.

## Summary

- resolve repeated Pi native session identities member by member instead of failing the whole inventory
- admit the longest member when every other member is an exact byte prefix of it, and bind no leaf for the covered copies
- quarantine all members of an identity whose records diverge, with one deterministic diagnostic, as Claude discovery does
- add regression tests for identical copies, a continued copy, a rewritten OMP title slot, and divergent copies

## Why

OMP copies a session's subagent transcripts into sessions continued or forked from it, and the copies keep the original `session` header. Pi discovery returned `InvalidPayload("Pi inventory repeats a native session identity")` on the first repeated identity with a different observation, so one copied transcript removed every Pi session from the route. #1226 has a synthetic reproduction.

In practice those copies are not conflicting: each one is the same file, or a prefix of the copy that kept growing after the session was continued. Admitting the longest member keeps every record. Covered copies get no leaf and no rejection, which is how discovery already treated a member whose observation equals the selected one. That keeps the inventory complete, so deletions stay certifiable. Quarantining copies instead would mark the route partial for as long as OMP keeps them, which is permanent.

The comparison runs only for repeated identities. It reopens both members through the retained authority (`reopen_same_object`), reads up to the shorter member's observed length, and skips a leading OMP title slot when both members start with one, because OMP rewrites that slot in place. A short read maps to `SourceChangedDuringCapture`; any other read failure rejects that member through the existing `reject_unreadable_file` path.

Members whose records diverge cannot be merged safely, so they follow the Claude discovery contract: every member is rejected with `with_quarantined_source`, and the member at the first path carries the logical diagnostic. Peers in the route still publish.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared` (4 new tests in `pi/nativepath/source_backed/discovery/tests.rs`)
- `cargo test -p ctx-history-capture-composition-qualification -p ctx-history-source-discovery -p ctx-history-source-discovery-qualification -p ctx-history-jsonl`
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared`
- the reproduction in #1226 fails on 2.5.0 and lists both sessions with this branch
- against a real OMP sessions directory in a temporary data root: 2.5.0 fails the route immediately; this branch indexes 2,731 sessions in 203 s, with one unrelated non-session JSONL file quarantined as before
- no new files or dependencies; I have not run the Bazel build locally

title: 2.5.0: one appended session still fails the whole provider import (provider source changed during bounded capture)
body:
## Summary

`provider source changed during bounded capture` still fails a whole provider in ctx 2.5.0 when a single session file is appended during an incremental import. This is the same behaviour as #1068 (closed as completed, no linked change), so I am reopening it as a new report against 2.5.0.

## Environment

- ctx 2.5.0 managed install, macOS (Apple Silicon), manual indexing mode, daemon not persistent.
- Claude Code history ~9k sessions, Pi ~6.4k sessions, on an APFS external volume (real paths, no symlinks).
- Command run once per day:

```text
ctx --data-root <root> import --incremental --provider claude --no-blame --format json --progress none --path <claude projects dir>
```

## What happens

While other agent sessions are running, the import exits 1 after ~50 s:

```text
Error: 1 import source failed; first failure: provider source changed during bounded capture
```

Because `--path` selects exactly one source, the whole provider is kept at its previous index. A retry after 15 s usually succeeds, but under sustained activity three attempts in a row can fail (seen for the Pi provider), so that day's new sessions never land.

## Expected

One actively appended session should not hold back every other session of the same provider. Either of these would fix it:

1. Capture append-only JSONL files up to the last complete line seen at capture start and pick up the rest on the next import; or
2. Fail (or skip) only the changed session, publish the rest of the provider, and report the skipped session in the JSON receipt so callers can retry just that one.

An opt-in flag (e.g. `--skip-changed-sessions`) would be fine if changing the default is undesirable.

Related: #1068, #283, #631, #662.

title: `pi` importer leaves `agent_scope` unset, excluding Pi sessions from `--scope primary` and `--primary-only`
body:
### Environment

- `ctx`: `2.5.0` (commit `0b117cbac`, current `main`)
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Data root: explicit `--data-root` (temporary directory)
- Provider / source format: `pi` / `pi_session_jsonl`

### What happens

In `ctx 2.5.0`, events imported from Pi (`--provider pi`) have `"agent_scope": null` instead of `"primary"`.

Because both `ctx list events --scope primary` and `ctx search --primary-only` require `event.agent_scope == Some(CoreAgentScope::Primary)`, every Pi session is excluded from primary-scoped queries. The same happens after `ctx archive export` and `ctx archive restore`, which preserve `"agent_scope": null`.

In `crates/ctx-history-providers-jsonl-shared/src/provider/providers/pi/nativepath/source_backed.rs` (lines 357-400), `CoreRecord::new_selected(...)` initializes `agent_scope` to `None` and the Pi projector never assigns `Some(AgentScope::Primary)`, unlike other native providers (such as `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `antigravity`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `goose`, `kiro`, `cline`, and `warp`).

Query filters that require an explicit `Primary` scope:
- `crates/ctx-history-index-query/src/event_range/selection.rs` (lines 219-225) and `crates/ctx-history-index-query/src/event_range.rs` (lines 895-907)
- `crates/ctx-history-index-query/src/filtering/core_match.rs` (lines 69-73) and `crates/ctx-history-index-query/src/filtering.rs` (lines 236-250, 585-598)

By contrast, `ctx sessions --no-subagents` (`crates/ctx-history-index-query/src/execution/session_list.rs`, lines 248-287) excludes `AgentScope::Subagent`, `delegated`/`workflow_child` relationships, and non-fork/non-resume parented sessions while retaining unscoped root and forked sessions, so it still lists Pi sessions.

### How to reproduce

Tested on `ctx 2.5.0` using a synthetic session in a temporary directory:

```sh
run_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$run_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$run_dir/data" "$run_dir/pi/--tmp-demo--"

cat > "$run_dir/data/config.toml" <<'TOML'
[analytics]
enabled = false

[indexing]
mode = "manual"

[search]
semantic = false

[upgrade]
auto = "off"

[sources]
automatic = false

[blame]
enabled = false
TOML

cat > "$run_dir/pi/--tmp-demo--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01950000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001.jsonl" <<'JSONL'
{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"01950000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001","timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/tmp/demo"}
{"type":"message","id":"a1b2c3d4","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:01.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"canary-pi-scope-repro"}]}}
{"type":"message","id":"b2c3d4e5","parentId":"a1b2c3d4","timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:02.000Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"confirmed-pi-scope-repro"}]}}
JSONL

ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" import --provider pi --path "$run_dir/pi" --no-blame --progress none --format json >/dev/null

# Returns 2 events, both with "agent_scope": null
ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" list events --scope all --format json

# Returns 0 events
ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" list events --scope primary --format json

# Returns 1 result
ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" search "canary-pi-scope-repro" --refresh off --format json

# Returns 0 results
ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" search "canary-pi-scope-repro" --primary-only --refresh off --format json

# Returns 1 session
ctx --data-root "$run_dir/data" sessions --no-subagents --format json
```

Exporting and restoring that data root (`ctx archive export` followed by `ctx archive restore`) preserves `"agent_scope": null`, so `list events --scope primary` and `search --primary-only` return `0` on the restored archive as well.

### Expected behavior

Primary Pi sessions should be returned by `ctx list events --scope primary` and `ctx search --primary-only`, consistent with other native providers.

For Pi sessions, `crates/ctx-history-read-application/tests/support/search_show/pi_flow.rs` currently asserts `record.agent_scope == None` (from #856, which avoided inferring `agent_scope` for OMP `parentSession` forks), and OMP can also place subagent transcripts under `<session>/<Agent>.jsonl` (as noted in #1226). Setting `core.agent_scope = Some(AgentScope::Primary)` on primary Pi sessions (while handling any OMP subagent transcripts separately, or leaving them non-primary) would align Pi with other native providers without pulling subagent transcripts into primary-only queries.

title: fix(history): avoid redundant work for unchanged Zstd archives
body:
A full route refresh copied and decompressed Zstd JSONL archives even when they matched a previously certified generation. One no-op refresh wrote about 31 MB for a 1.03 MB archive that expanded to 30.02 MB. Adding an unrelated raw sibling repeated the work.

Reuse the existing admission proof during first-record classification when the archive matches a certified generation. New and changed archives still undergo physical validation.

**Verification**

- Lifecycle regression passed for a no-op refresh, adding a sibling, and replacing the archive. The replacement’s new content was indexed.
- All 143 JSONL unit tests passed.
- macOS Cargo provider lifecycle suite: 106 passed, 5 failed. All five failures reproduced on the unmodified base: one OpenClaw and four Lingma-related.
- Pinned Bazel run was interrupted during analysis and toolchain fetching, before tests ran.

title: OpenCode 2 upgrade still fails on 2.5.0: overlap proof rejects unmigrated rows and file/agent parts (follow-up to #1105)
body:
## Summary

This follows up #1105, which was closed as fixed by #1109. On ctx 2.5.0, an OpenCode database upgraded from 1.x to 2 is still rejected as a whole:

```text
(opencode, unreadable, retained prior data): invalid capture payload: OpenCode NativePath found ambiguous populated message schema families: session_message_seq, message_part
```

Since #1109, `select_schema_family` picks `session_message` only when `overlap::legacy_is_covered` proves that v2 holds everything v1 does. On this database the proof fails for two separate reasons, and selection falls through to the ambiguity error. Neither layout contains the other, so as far as I can tell an upgraded database with these rows can never be imported.

The 29 Oct comment on #1105 ("I'm on 2.3.0 and I still get this") may be the same case.

## Environment

- ctx 2.5.0
- OpenCode 2.4.1, upgraded from 1.x
- `message`, `part` and `session_message` are populated; `session_part` is empty.
- Before the upgrade, ctx indexed this source as `opencode-family-message_part-v1`.

## Where the proof fails

### 1. OpenCode's migration skipped some v1 messages

I ran the pairing join from `legacy_is_covered` in SQL (match by id, or by `parentID` for assistant `summary` messages). 113 v1 messages have no `session_message` row, although all their sessions exist in `session_v2`:

```sql
select count(*)
from message m
where not exists (select 1 from session_message n where n.id = m.id)
  and not (json_extract(m.data, '$.role') = 'assistant'
           and json_extract(m.data, '$.summary') = 1
           and exists (select 1 from session_message n
                       where n.id = json_extract(m.data, '$.parentID')));
-- 113
```

They are all subtask or compaction turns:

| v1 message | Part types | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| user | subtask | 31 |
| assistant | tool | 31 |
| user | compaction (4 also have text) | 27 |
| assistant, `summary: true` | none, or text / step-start / patch | 24 |

Each of these fails the pairing check at [`overlap.rs:69`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-sqlite-logical/src/providers/opencode/native_path/overlap.rs#L69).

### 2. v1 has part types the proof never accepts

`Coverage::part` returns `false` for any part type outside its list ([`overlap.rs:208-216`](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-sqlite-logical/src/providers/opencode/native_path/overlap.rs#L208-L216), and the `_ => false` under "Subtask/file and unknown mappings need their own lossless proof" at [line 351](https://github.com/ctxrs/ctx/blob/v2.5.0/crates/ctx-history-providers-sqlite-logical/src/providers/opencode/native_path/overlap.rs#L351)). Messages that do pair contain:

| Part type | Parts | Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | 2,823 | 2,329 |
| `agent` | 117 | 110 |

The `subtask` parts are all on the unpaired messages above. So one file attachment anywhere in an upgraded database is enough to fail the proof.

I only checked part types; I did not evaluate the per-part JSON checks (`has_only_keys`, text flags, metadata), so other conditions may fail too.

### v1 is not a superset either

Some `session_message` rows of type `system` and `synthetic` have no v1 counterpart.

## Impact

- `ctx import` exits 1 on every run and reports the source as unreadable.
- Search keeps serving the data indexed before the upgrade. Per #1105, OpenCode 2 stops writing v1 after the upgrade, so new OpenCode sessions would never be indexed.

## Suggested behavior

Any of these would unblock upgraded databases. I don't know which fits the fail-closed policy best:

1. Import the union: every v2 row, plus v1 messages with no v2 counterpart, plus v1 parts that v2 can't represent (`file`, `agent`, `subtask`) attached to their paired message.
2. When the proof fails and the source was last accepted as `message_part`, keep reading `message_part` while v1 is unchanged. This only helps databases nobody writes to any more, so it's a stopgap.
3. At minimum, say which check failed and how many rows it affected. The current message is identical to #1105, so it reads as if the fix didn't ship.

title: Feature request: persistent named roots for provider history (consistency with other providers)
body:
# Feature request: persistent named roots for provider history

## Problem

CTX supports exact-path imports for native providers, and named roots exist for providers with configured-root support. Users cannot yet register an application-owned or relocated location once and have CTX keep importing new conversations automatically.

Each harness can store history in a known provider format in a different location. The location is stable for that installation or profile, but CTX's default discovery may not know it.

The existing exact-path workflow works as a one-time operation. It requires the user to repeat the path for later imports and does not register a location for ongoing refresh.

## Motivation

Users should be able to tell CTX once where a provider-owned history root is located and then have CTX maintain that source normally.

The basic workflow is:

```text
register the location once
import existing history
watch the location for new or changed sessions
search all retained conversations through CTX
```

This should apply to relocated or application-owned copies of formats CTX already supports. It should work without a custom exporter, runtime hook, MCP server, or app-specific integration.

## Existing context

CTX supports one-shot native imports:

```text
ctx import --provider <provider> --path <path>
```

CTX also supports named roots for providers whose configured-root capability is enabled:

```text
ctx sources add <name> --provider <provider> --root <path>
```

For existing providers, the root capability determines whether the configured path expands to provider-specific session trees or is treated as one exact file or directory.

The gap is that users with an alternate location for an already-supported provider need a durable, refreshable root that remains associated with the provider format and profile.

## Validation evidence

A recent validation found both existing native routes useful:

- A Codex rollout tree can be discovered under a known native default and imported by exact rollout path.
- A relocated Claude project JSONL tree can be recognized as a Claude project tree when the configured root resolves to the directory containing `projects`.
- Claude assistant records can carry an effective model ID, such as `claude-opus-5-5`, plus effort and speed metadata.

The validation also found a root-expansion edge to cover:

- A Claude configured root is provider-home based and resolves to `<provider-home>/projects`.
- Registering `<provider-home>/projects/projects` by supplying the already-expanded project directory can report the source as missing.
- The named-root contract should define whether a root is provider-home, a project tree, or an exact session file and should avoid appending provider subdirectories twice.

No provider authentication, cloud history, or app-specific runtime hook was needed for this native-format validation.

## Desired behavior

- Allow a named root to be registered once for an already-supported provider format.
- Allow the root to point at the provider-owned directory or file containing history.
- Preserve provider identity and native session/event identity.
- Preserve the provider format separately from the location.
- Add existing history during registration or the next explicit refresh.
- Continue refreshing when sessions are appended or files are changed.
- Detect deleted, rewritten, replaced, and moved sessions deterministically.
- Preserve stable session and event citations across refreshes.
- Remain read-only with respect to the provider-owned source.
- Keep independent profiles or accounts in separate named roots.
- Leave missing roots visible and report `configured_root_missing`.
- Allow a missing root to be restored or replaced under the same name.
- Avoid silently merging separate locations, workspaces, accounts, or profiles.
- Keep credentials and private provider state outside the source contract.
- Expose source state, refresh state, format, and skipped-record diagnostics through CLI and machine-readable output.

Example intent:

```text
ctx sources add <name> --provider <provider> --root <path>
ctx search "topic" --provider <provider>
```

The final command names and configuration syntax are implementation decisions.

## Format scope

The proposal is specifically about persistent location registration and refresh for formats CTX already recognizes.

Examples include:

- A relocated Codex rollout tree or exact rollout file.
- A relocated Claude project JSONL tree.
- A relocated supported JSONL, JSON, or SQLite history layout.
- An application-owned profile that contains an existing supported provider format.

This proposal does not require a new provider format adapter by itself.

If the selected files do not match an existing CTX format, CTX should report that the format is unsupported or unavailable. A generic custom-history importer or a new native adapter can remain a separate feature.

## Provider and format separation

Provider identity and source format may be different:

| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Provider | Stable namespace for the history producer |
| Source ID | Stable name for the registered location or profile |
| Source format | Existing CTX format used to parse provider-owned history |
| Location kind | Directory tree or exact file |
| Refresh mode | Manual or watched incremental refresh |

A harness should not be assumed to change provider format based only on model choice. A Codex-model run and Claude-model run should be distinguished only when the stored history files prove the provider format and metadata.

## Suggested implementation paths

1. Reuse the existing configured-root registration and exact-path importer seams.
2. Attach a named root to the existing provider format rather than introducing a catch-all parser.
3. Register the current location as one source and enable normal daemon refresh.
4. Preserve source identity through append, rewrite, replacement, and no-op scans.
5. Add missing-root, incompatible-format, profile-separation, and skipped-record diagnostics.
6. Add deterministic fixtures for Codex and Claude relocated roots.
7. Verify that identical relocated files produce stable logical identities and no duplicate sessions.
8. Document persistent roots, refresh behavior, format scope, and privacy boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can register a relocated or application-owned root once.
- [ ] Existing sessions at that root are imported during registration or the next supported refresh.
- [ ] New sessions and appended events are found by normal CTX refresh.
- [ ] Rewritten or replaced sessions are reconciled without duplicate sessions or events.
- [ ] Deleted sessions are reconciled according to existing provider retention and refresh policy.
- [ ] A missing root remains named and reports its missing state.
- [ ] Replacing the missing root with a compatible location restores refresh under the same name.
- [ ] Separate profiles or accounts remain separate sources.
- [ ] The source uses the existing provider parser and format contract.
- [ ] Provider-native session and event IDs remain stable where the format exposes them.
- [ ] Cwd, timestamps, roles, tool output, and model metadata remain available where the provider exposes them.
- [ ] Search, show, citations, event streaming, and source status work normally after refresh.
- [ ] The provider-owned root is never modified or treated as CTX-owned storage.
- [ ] Machine-readable output reports location, format, refresh, missing, and skipped-record state.
- [ ] Public fixtures contain no credentials, private paths, or identifying data.

## Privacy and data boundaries

The feature should remain local and read-only.

- It must not execute a command to discover or import history.
- It must not upload provider history.
- It must not copy provider-private binary payloads or opaque blobs into Core.
- It must not silently merge profiles or accounts.
- It must make missing, moved, unreadable, and incompatible sources visible.

Credentials and private provider state remain outside the source contract.

## Risks

- A provider profile can contain multiple locations or formats.
- A named root can disappear or be replaced by an incompatible directory or file.
- Live refresh can miss a rewrite or observe a partially written file.
- Reusing one name can accidentally merge independent profiles.
- Provider formats can migrate or add fields that CTX reads differently.
- A native adapter may need schema-version or format-compatibility checks.

## Scope

This request adds persistent named roots and incremental refresh for already-supported provider formats stored at a non-default location.

It does not require:

- adding a brand-new provider format adapter;
- replacing existing native provider importers;
- cloud history synchronization;
- provider authentication;
- automatic account enrollment;
- automatic private-memory classification;
- command-based exporter execution;
- a vendor-specific or application-specific provider namespace.
